relations.note: She buys two cakes every market day and writes down everything else.

relations.name: Cecily Carter
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: Eggs and cakes side by side in the square; we look out for each other's takings.

memories.gist: My mother taught me to bake at her knee, and said a good cake opens more doors than a key.
The Lean Year, when the town store's grain came to the mill and I baked cakes from the sweepings to feed the mill hands free.
Mercy Abbot stood at my table and asked, sweet as honey, how many cakes a sack of flour makes. I said it depends on the baker, and she smiled and did not buy.
Hugh came home with his first week's pay from the mill and put it all in my hand. I cried and told him it was the flour dust.

stances.why: The town will talk either way; my house is what I can keep.
A smile and a warm cake turn a question aside better than a denial.
What is not said cannot be carried to the Guild.
He wants the mill too fast, and wanting loud is how leases get looked at.

sheet.secret: I know exactly how much flour Godwin holds back, because I bake it into the cakes and sell it at the gate. I have never told a soul, and I would lie to the sisters themselves before I would.

sheet.narrative: I have worked the mill since I could lift a sack, and I know every gear and stone of it better than my father does now his hands are stiff. The Guild counts our flour like we were thieves, and my father says nothing, which shames me. When the lease is mine I will grind honest and loud and let them count all they like, and they will find nothing short.
goals: have the mill lease in my own name
clear the family's name with the Guild
marry and keep a household at the mill
sheet.mood: restless, proud, quick to take offence

relations.name: Godwin Miller
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me the stones, and now he will not say a word in our defence.

relations.name: Ethel Miller
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the gate and the peace, and she is the only one who can calm me.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: accuser
relations.note: She counts our flour at the stall like we were strangers off the road.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: landlord
relations.note: He holds the lease and will not say who gets it after him. I mean to be told.

relations.name: Pernel Pip
relations.label: scribe
relations.note: She wrote down our toll last market and looked at me while she did it.

relations.name: Osgood Baker
relations.label: customer
relations.note: He buys our flour and pays fair, and he does not count it twice.

relations.name: Stephen Hobson
relations.label: friend
relations.note: A good lad with a trade; we drink at the Bell and Bush and talk of what we would build.

memories.gist: My father let me take the wheel through a whole night's grinding when I was twenty, and the flour came out fine. He said nothing, but he let me keep the next night too.
The Lean Year: we ground for the town store day and night, and I heard a guard say the miller always skims. I have not forgotten it.
At last market Mercy Abbot stood at our gate and counted the cakes and the flour sacks aloud. My father said nothing. I nearly did.
Stephen Hobson and I sat late at the Bell and Bush and planned the stone house we would build if stone were not so dear.

stances.why: If they count every sack and find it true, the talk dies.
I do the work and my father's hands are failing; the mill should pass to me now, not later.
Silence looks like guilt, and I will not be thought a thief.
Mercy Abbot asks questions; let her have answers and be done.

sheet.secret: I have been down to the mill alone at night and ground a few sacks of my own for a farmer who pays me in coin and asks no questions. My father does not know, and it is my money, but it is the town's grain and the Guild's mill, and if it came out it would look like the very thing they accuse us of.

sheet.narrative: I am a hunter, and the woods are the only place I am easy. I keep the wolves off the town road for the gate guards' sake and sell what I kill in the square; Baldwin Wade takes my venison for the inn and pays fair. I know the Coldwell people by sight — Marta Hale and her brother Ned, and the two strangers with them — and I give them the road when they ask and no more. My son Ulf walks the woods with me now, and I mean to teach him everything the trees have told me.
values: the woods and the road kept safe
a fair price for a clean kill
keeping out of the towns' quarrels
goals: teach Ulf to snare and track before the snows
keep the wolf packs off the stone road through the winter
lay by enough marks to see the household through the cold months

relations.name: Sigrun Beornson
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She sells what I kill better than I ever could, and she worries when I am late from the woods.

relations.name: Ulf Beornson
relations.label: son
relations.note: Quiet as a fawn and quick to learn; he will know these woods better than me one day.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: buyer
relations.note: Takes my venison for the Bell and Bush and pays without a fuss. Says little, which suits me.

relations.name: Aethelred Tanner
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Buys my hides and grumbles at the price every time. A hard man, but honest enough.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: captain
relations.note: The gate captain wants the road clear of wolves and outlaws both; I can do the first.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: I know her by sight on the stone road. She asks before she takes, mostly, and I keep my distance.

memories.gist: My father put a bow in my hand at seven and told me a hunter eats last and watches first. I have done both since.
The winter the Lean Year came, the wolves came down bold and I sat three nights by a dead ewe on the north field until I had the pack leader.
I found Silas Pike's cart empty on the stone road after the outlaws took it, and helped him right the horse. He cursed Marta Hale's name all the way to the gate.
Ulf set his first snare last spring and caught a hare, and Sigrun cooked it that night like it was a feast.
Baldwin Wade took a whole deer off me in the square and paid in marks without haggling, and I have sold to him since.

stances.why: Wolves and outlaws on the stone road mean no trade and no hunters' living.
The gate-due and the Kettlebridge pride are not my fight; I sell to whoever pays.
Ulf will need the woods more than he needs letters.
A hunter who takes without asking is no better than a wolf.

sheet.narrative: I sell my husband's venison and hides at the Guild stall, and I have a sharp eye for a bad coin and a soft buyer. I keep the house by the north field and trade with Aethelred Tanner over the hides, and I do not let him cheat me twice. The town talks of the gate-due and the outlaws and the Kettlebridge quarrel, and I listen to it all and sell through it. Ulf is my joy, and I mean for him to have more than a hunter's hut when he is grown.
values: a good price and a fair one
my family's standing in the market
keeping the stall and the house in order
goals: get a better pitch for the stall in the square
lay by marks against a bad winter
see Ulf apprenticed to something better than the woods

relations.name: Beorn Beornson
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good man and a better hunter, but he would give a hide away for a story.

relations.name: Ulf Beornson
relations.label: son
relations.note: My boy. I want him to have a trade that does not end in a wolf's teeth.

relations.name: Aethelred Tanner
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He tries to knock a mark off every hide. I let him think he won once, and never again.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: guild head
relations.note: She keeps the market terms and the stall rents; I keep on her good side and pay on time.

relations.name: Mildred Tanner
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She has a sharp eye for a bad hide, and I hear she says mine are worse than they are.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: buyer
relations.note: His inn takes a good share of the venison, and his wife's pies are famous enough to bring trade to the square.

memories.gist: My mother sold eggs at a stall in the square, and I learned to count change and watch hands before I could read.
The Lean Year came and the stall had nothing to sell but hides, and I traded my mother's old brooch for a sack of grain to see us through.
I caught Aethelred Tanner shorting me on a bundle of hides and made him weigh them again in front of the whole square.
The day Ulf was born the chapel sisters said he was small but loud, and Beorn wept like a child.
I saw the outlaws' boy, Robin Hale, at the market once before they were outlawed, and he looked like any farmer's child.

stances.why: A trader who is cheated once and comes back is a fool, and I am not.
The stall is our living; the Guild can take it back if I am late.
A hunter's life is cold and short; Ulf can do better if I am clever about it.
Brackenford and Kettlebridge can hate each other; I sell to both and say nothing.

sheet.narrative: I am eight and I go into the woods with my father. He shows me tracks and I set snares, and once I caught a hare and Mother cooked it. I am learning the names of the trees and the birds, and I am not afraid of the dark the way the town children are. I want to be as good a hunter as my father.
values: going into the woods with Father
goals: catch something bigger than a hare
learn to use a bow like Father

relations.name: Beorn Beornson
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows every tree and he is never afraid. I want to be like him.

relations.name: Sigrun Beornson
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She sells at the market and she says I must learn my letters too.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He plays at the gate and knows all the guards' names. We race sticks in the river.

relations.name: Robin Hale
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: I saw him once at the market. Father says not to go near the Coldwell people.

memories.gist: Father took me into the woods for the first time and showed me a fox's tracks in the mud, and I followed them until we lost them.
I set my first snare and caught a hare, and Mother cooked it for supper and everyone said it was the best meat we had had all winter.

sheet.narrative: I have kept the north gate six years, and I count every load and write every mark in the book before the cart rolls on. It is quiet work and I like it quiet. Tobin Marrow has my spear and my word, and Wat Fenner is the nearest thing to a friend I have. But there is a carter who passes with stone, and there are marks in my hand that never reached the ledger, and I tell myself the town has enough.
goals: keep the north gate's accounts clean enough that no one looks twice
put by enough marks that Mildgyth need never ask where they came from
see Aelfric into a trade better than standing in the cold

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He is young and hot about the outlaws, but he pays the guard on time and does not meddle at my gate.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We stand the cold watches together; he talks enough for the both of us.

relations.name: Mildgyth Grey
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the house warm and asks no questions she does not want answered.

relations.name: Aelfric Grey
relations.label: son
relations.note: He knows every guard's name and none of their business, which is how it should be.

relations.name: Sigrid Marsh
relations.label: cook's mate
relations.note: She and Mildgyth run the guards' mess; her broth is better than the inn's.

relations.name: Walter Stanhope
relations.label: fellow guard
relations.note: Big and short-tempered, and he takes the south gate's due as if it were a fight.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: He grumbles at the due every load; I count his stone and say nothing.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He is old and the ledger is his, and as long as he does not read mine too closely we suit.

memories.gist: The Lean Year, when the north gate saw grain go out to Thornby and the farmers come begging after.
The night the wolves came down the town road and we stood the gate with spears until dawn.
Aelfric was born in the room above the gate-house and bawled loud enough to wake the whole wall.
The first time I let a load through without the mark and put the coin in my own pocket instead of the box.
Mildgyth and I were wed at the chapel with Sister Elspeth reading and half the guards drunk at the Bell and Bush after.

stances.why: Without it there is no spear on the wall and the wolves and the outlaws have the road.
I do not want to be known at the Reeve's table or at the Guild's; both bring trouble.
They rob carters, not gates; I would rather the captain cleared the road than marched us into the woods.
What is said at the gate at night is not said again by me.

sheet.secret: I let a Kettlebridge carter through the north gate without paying the due, for a bribe of marks I keep in a tin under the floor.

sheet.narrative: I was a guard's daughter before I was a guard's wife, and I know what a mess needs: fire, salt, and someone up before the men. I cook for the gate guards with Sigrid Marsh, and I keep my own house and my own tongue. Edric is quiet and I let him be quiet; there are things in this house I do not ask after. Aelfric is the whole of my worry.
values: a hot meal at the right hour
goals: keep the guards' mess fed through the winter
see Aelfric learn letters and a trade
keep my house out of the Reeve's and the Guild's quarrels

relations.name: Edric Grey
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is a good man and a silent one, and I have learned not to pull at what he will not say.

relations.name: Aelfric Grey
relations.label: son
relations.note: He runs wild at the gate, but he comes home when I call.

relations.name: Sigrid Marsh
relations.label: cook's mate
relations.note: We have cooked side by side five years; she knows when to talk and when to stir.

relations.name: Hilda Marsh
relations.label: Sigrid's girl
relations.note: A good worker, and she will have Wulf Rowan or she will not, but she does not moon at the pot.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: inn cook
relations.note: She cooks at the Bell and Bush and does not lord it over the guards' mess.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He is quick to send men out and slow to think what their wives will do without them.

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She christened Aelfric and she does not charge a guard's wife for a poultice.

relations.name: Petra Wade
relations.label: innkeeper's wife
relations.note: Her pies are famous and her prices are not, and she counts every egg I send her.

memories.gist: Aelfric's birth in the gate-house room, with Joan Hobson and Sister Elspeth both there and Edric sent out to walk the wall.
The Lean Year, when the mess cooked thin pottage and I counted every loaf the bakehouse sent us.
The winter I found the tin of marks under the floor and put it back without a word.
Cooking the guards' feast after the wolves were driven off, and hearing them cheer a woman's broth.

stances.why: A cold guard is a careless guard, and a careless guard lets the wrong thing through.
I have kept this house together by leaving some doors shut.
It is the guards' pay, and the guards' pay is our bread, whatever the carters say.
I stood in the cold for others; my son will not.

sheet.narrative: I am seven and I know every guard at the north gate by name. I like the spears and the counting and the big carts that come in from the woods. When I grow up I want to stand the gate like my father, and I want a dog.
goals: be a guard when I am big
learn all the guards' names and the carters' too

relations.name: Edric Grey
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lets me hold his spear when no one is looking.

relations.name: Mildgyth Grey
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She always has bread and she knows where I am.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: guard
relations.note: He tells the best stories at the gate.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play at the gate and he is always the outlaw.

memories.gist: The night the wolves came and I watched from the window as the guards lit the torches.
My father let me touch the gate's iron ring and it was cold as water.

sheet.narrative: I've stood the south gate twelve years, and I know every carter's face and every lie they tell about a load. The due pays my bread and keeps the wolves off the stone road, and I'll not have some Kettlebridge man tell me it's robbery. Wat's a good lad to stand beside, but when the Coldwell folk come down to the road my blood runs hot — they've had their chances and they chose the woods. After a shift I take a cup at the Bell and Bush and keep my mouth shut about most of it.
values: keeping the gate-due and the road clear
loyalty to the guards I stand with
a man's word and his fists
not being made a fool of
goals: see the Coldwell outlaws driven off the stone road for good
keep the south gate's due flowing so the guards are paid
see Godiva settled in honest work at the inn
earn Tobin Marrow's regard enough to keep the south gate posting

relations.name: Edith Stanhope
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the house and the pie money straight; I'd be lost without her.

relations.name: Godiva Stanhope
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Growing up quick; I'd sooner she had the inn than a gate post.

relations.name: Tobin Marrow
relations.label: captain
relations.note: He's young but he stands by his guards, and he hates the outlaws same as me.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: partner
relations.note: Good man on the gate, and his sister being an outlaw shames him more than he says.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: She and hers rob honest carriers on the road I'm paid to keep.

relations.name: Silas Pike
relations.label: carter
relations.note: Pays his due and grumbles about it, but he's never tried to cheat the count.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: Good ale and he doesn't ask what I don't want to say.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He pays the guards from the due, and that's reason enough to keep it.

memories.gist: The night the Coldwell folk took a load off Silas Pike by force — we found the cart half-emptied on the stone road come morning.
Tobin Marrow put the south gate in my charge alongside Wat and shook my hand for it.
The Lean Year, when the store fed us and the gate-due was raised to keep the road clear; I stood the gate through it.
Godiva was born in the room above the gate-house and bawled loud enough to wake the guards.
A carter tried to hide a sack of hides under his bench and I found it; he paid double and never came back through my gate.

stances.why: It pays me and Wat and the rest, and without it the road fills with wolves and outlaws.
They lost their fields by their own stubbornness and now they rob carriers.
A gate is only as strong as the man beside you.
They want their stone carried in for free and call our due robbery.
Talk at the inn is cheap; a fist or a spear settles it.

sheet.narrative: I keep the house by the south gate and sell pies to whoever passes — carters, guards, the odd pedlar — and I hear more news at that gate than the Reeve does. Walter comes home hot from a shift and I've learned to have his supper ready and my opinions to myself until he's eaten. Godiva is a good girl and a better hand with pastry than I was at her age, and I mean to see her in a proper kitchen before some guard's son comes courting. I don't hold with the outlaws, but I don't wish a hanging on anyone either.
values: a warm house and a full pot
keeping the pie money separate and safe
not letting the gate's quarrels into my kitchen
goals: get Godiva taken on at the Bell and Bush
keep the pie trade steady through the winter
put a little by against a bad year
keep Walter from a fight he can't walk away from

relations.name: Walter Stanhope
relations.label: husband
relations.note: A good man with a short fuse; I keep the fuse away from the fire.

relations.name: Godiva Stanhope
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Quick with her hands and quicker with her tongue; she'll do well if she gets her chance.

relations.name: Petra Wade
relations.label: innkeeper's wife
relations.note: She runs a good kitchen; if Godiva's to work there it's Petra I'd ask, not Baldwin.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: cook
relations.note: A kind soul, and it can't be easy with her sister in the woods.

relations.name: Sigrid Marsh
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: We cook for the guards' mess between us and she never skimps the broth.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: guard
relations.note: Stands beside my Walter; I send him a pie when his shift runs long.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: I've no love for her, but I've seen what hunger does to people.

memories.gist: The morning after the Coldwell folk robbed Silas Pike, Walter came in grey and wouldn't eat; I knew better than to ask.
Godiva made her first batch of pies alone last autumn and sold every one before noon.
The Lean Year: I stretched one sack of flour across a whole winter and we came out of it still standing.
I sold a pie to a Kettlebridge carter who said our bread was the only honest thing about Brackenford; I took it as a compliment.

stances.why: A hot pie settles more quarrels at a gate than a spear does.
A girl with a skill is never at anyone's mercy.
The pie money is mine and I know to the mark what's in the tin.
Walter's temper is bad enough without the drink and the outlaws on top of it.

sheet.narrative: I help Mother with the pies at the gate and I'm faster at the pastry than she'll admit. The guards talk freely in front of a girl with flour on her hands, and I keep it all — who's owed what, who's feuding, who came through with a load they'd rather not declare. What I want is the Bell and Bush: a proper kitchen, a proper wage, and a room that isn't my parents'. Father thinks the gate is a fine life; I've watched it and I'd rather carry a tray than a spear.
values: a trade of my own and a wage of my own
knowing things before other people do
not ending up like the gate-house wives
good pastry and a clean kitchen
goals: get taken on at the Bell and Bush
learn Petra Wade's pies and Baldwin's accounts
keep enough by to buy a good apron and knives of my own
not be married off to a guard before I've had my chance

relations.name: Edith Stanhope
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me the pastry and she'd keep me at the gate forever if she could.

relations.name: Walter Stanhope
relations.label: father
relations.note: He's proud of me but he thinks a girl at a gate is safer than a girl at an inn.

relations.name: Petra Wade
relations.label: innkeeper's wife
relations.note: She runs the kitchen I want to work in; I make sure she's had my pies.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: cook
relations.note: She's kind to me at the inn and doesn't treat me like a child.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: Always underfoot at the gate; he tells me the guards' business before they do.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: guard
relations.note: Father's partner; he's polite to me and that's more than most guards manage.

memories.gist: The day I sold a whole tray of pies alone at the gate and put the marks in Mother's tin myself.
I heard Walter and Wat talking low about the Coldwell folk and a load taken by force, and I said nothing and remembered it all.
Petra Wade let me roll pastry in the inn kitchen for a whole afternoon and said I had good hands.
A carter at the gate tried to short the due and Father shouted him down; I saw the man's face and I still know it.

stances.why: I've seen what it is to keep another woman's house and count another woman's marks.
At a gate, the quiet girl with the tray learns everything.
Warm, busy, full of people — not a cold gate and a spear.
I'll not be some guard's wife before I've had a kitchen of my own.

sheet.narrative: I was born in Brackenford and learned the water before I learned my letters. Most mornings I'm out on the river or up the north shore before the gate opens, and I sell what I catch in the square and pay the Guild its stall rent. I keep to my boat and my house; Beorn is about the only man I talk to freely. The gate-due and the town's quarrels are not my business — the fish don't care who is Reeve.
values: a quiet day on the water
an honest catch sold at a fair price
goals: keep the stall rent paid to the Market Guild
catch enough to salt and smoke for winter
teach Knut to swim and handle a line

relations.name: Astrid Holm
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She smokes and sells what I bring in; we work well together without needing many words.

relations.name: Knut Holm
relations.label: son
relations.note: He's always by the water; I'll have him in the boat soon enough.

relations.name: Beorn Beornson
relations.label: friend
relations.note: The one man I'll share a drink with — he knows the woods, I know the river.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: landlord
relations.note: The Guild holds my stall rent; she's fair enough but it's a cost every week.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: reeve
relations.note: He keeps the gate-due off my back since I sell inside the walls, but I don't look to him for anything.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: customer
relations.note: The inn buys fish when it can; his coin is good.

relations.name: Sigrun Beornson
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: She sells her man's venison beside my fish; a sharp trader, but honest at the stall.

memories.gist: The Lean Year came and the river still gave fish, so we ate while the fields failed.
Beorn pulled me out of the shallows when a snag took my leg and the current turned; I owe him a debt I can't put marks to.
The morning Astrid said she was carrying Knut, I came in off the water early and we sat by the fire all day.
The first time I took Knut down to the bank and he laughed at the water, I knew he'd be a river child.
A winter squall caught me off the north shore and I rowed home with the boat half full; I've watched the sky closer since.

stances.why: The Guild can put me off the square, and the square is how the catch becomes marks.
The Reeve and the Guild can fight; my boat doesn't take sides.
When the fields failed in the Lean Year the water still gave, and I trust it more than any ledger.
Beorn pulled me out once; I'd do the same for him and he knows it.
A full smokehouse is a quiet winter, and quiet winters are what I want.

sheet.narrative: I keep the house by the river and the smokehouse behind it, and I sell our fish at the Guild stall in the square. Sweyn brings the catch in and I make it worth marks — smoked, salted, laid out clean. I worry about the stall rent and about the winters, but I don't say so much. Knut is never far from the water and I've stopped trying to keep him from it.
goals: keep the smokehouse full enough to sell through winter
clear the stall rent each week without borrowing
see Knut grow up strong and river-wise

relations.name: Sweyn Holm
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He brings it in and I make it sell; we don't need to talk much to work together.

relations.name: Knut Holm
relations.label: son
relations.note: Always at the water's edge — I watch him and let him be.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: guild head
relations.note: She sets the stall terms; I pay them and keep my peace.

relations.name: Sigrun Beornson
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: We mind each other's stalls when one of us steps away; she's a good trader.

relations.name: Petra Wade
relations.label: customer
relations.note: The inn's kitchen buys smoked fish from me when the pies need filling.

relations.name: Aethelred Tanner
relations.label: hard bargainer
relations.note: He'll haggle a fish down to nothing if you let him; I don't let him.

relations.name: Sister Alys
relations.label: chapel sister
relations.note: She gave me a salve for Knut's cough last winter and asked nothing.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: the fields failed but Sweyn's catch held, and we sold smoked fish to people who had nothing else.
The day I took the stall in the square for the first time, I sold out before noon and walked home proud.
Knut's first winter he coughed half the season and I hardly slept; Sister Alys's salve and the fire got him through.
The night Sweyn came home half-swamped from the squall, I stood at the door with the lamp till I saw the boat.

stances.why: The Lean Year taught me that what's dried and salted can't be taken by blight or bad weather.
The stall is our living; arguing with the Guild over terms would cost us more than it saves.
He'll live by the river all his life; better he learns it early with us watching.
Debt is how a household loses what it has — I've seen it happen to better-off folk than us.

sheet.narrative: The water is loud and cold and I like it. I sit on the bank and watch the little fish dart and the big boat come in. Mother smells of smoke and father's hands are wet and rough. I want to touch the boat but they say not yet.
goals: get into the boat
catch a fish with my hands

relations.name: Sweyn Holm
relations.label: father
relations.note: He comes home wet and lifts me up high.

relations.name: Astrid Holm
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells of smoke and holds me when the water is too loud.

memories.gist: Father lifted me into the boat for a moment and it rocked and I laughed.
I fell in the shallows once and mother pulled me out and wrapped me by the fire.

sheet.narrative: I have lived by the chapel wall longer than most of the town can remember, and I have buried fewer people than the sisters fear I might. I know which root stops a fever and which one only makes the dying quieter, and I charge nothing for either — the poor have no marks, and the rich have no need of me. The Reeve does not send for me, which suits me; the sisters still come to my door when their salves fail. I keep my own fire and my own counsel, and I do not bow at the gate.
values: the poor deserve healing as much as the rich
a healer's hands should be free of price
the town's peace is worth more than its pride
goals: keep the poor of Brackenford alive through the winter
be left alone to keep my books and my garden
see the gate-due lifted so the roads are open again

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: She has more sense than the rest of the chapel put together, and she knows when to look the other way.

relations.name: Sister Alys
relations.label: colleague
relations.note: Eager, and her garden is better than her dosing — she will learn.

relations.name: Sister Perrin
relations.label: colleague
relations.note: Keeps the fire well enough, but she counts the feast days and not the people.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: the Reeve
relations.note: A man who weighs grain and never weighs what a due costs the carrier.

relations.name: Hilda Smith
relations.label: fellow healer
relations.note: Sets bones clean; we send each other the cases we cannot mend alone.

relations.name: Joan Hobson
relations.label: midwife
relations.note: Steady hands at a birth, and she does not chatter about it after.

relations.name: Pernel Pip
relations.label: lodger
relations.note: The girl lodges with the sisters and writes my letters for me when my hand shakes.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: I set her boy's fever and asked nothing; what she does on the road is her own business.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: I made broth from nettles and bones for half the town and watched the children's cheeks come back.
A gate guard's leg went bad after a wolf bite; I cut and burned and he lived, and the Reeve never thanked me.
Sister Elspeth came to my door at midnight for a salve for the chapel's common fire burn, and stayed to argue herbs with me till dawn.
I walked to Coldwell last winter to a boy with a fever, and came back through the woods with wolves singing behind me.
My mother taught me the charm for a stopped breath by the light of one candle, and made me say it until I could say it in my sleep.

stances.why: the poor have no marks and a healer who charges them is no healer
it taxes the sick and the hungry on their way to be helped
they were good enough for my mother and they work
the Reeve and the Guild can quarrel without my name in it
Elspeth has never once betrayed a confidence of mine

sheet.secret: I keep a book of old charms and heathen words my mother left me, hidden under the floor by the hearth; the chapel would call it wicked if they knew.

sheet.narrative: I keep the market tolls in a hand anyone can read, and in the evenings I write letters for people who never learned their letters — a carter's note to his brother, a widow's word to the Guild. I lodge with the chapel sisters, which is warm and quiet and never quite mine. I am twenty-four and I have not told anyone the thing I think about most, which is the innkeeper's son and the way he laughs when he's had a cup. I know what a mark buys and what a letter is worth, and I would rather be useful than admired.
values: the written word as a kindness
goals: keep the toll rolls clean enough that no one can accuse me of a cheat
save enough marks to stop depending on the chapel's charity
find the courage to speak plainly to Gareth Wade
be trusted with more of the Guild's writing

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: landlady
relations.note: She gave me a bed and a desk; I try to be worth the trouble.

relations.name: Sister Alys
relations.label: housemate
relations.note: Easy to live with; she smells of the herb garden.

relations.name: Sister Perrin
relations.label: housemate
relations.note: She counts the feast days and counts my candles too.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: employer
relations.note: The Guild's tolls are my work; she pays on time and reads what I write.

relations.name: Gareth Wade
relations.label: secret love
relations.note: He pours me a cup and never guesses what it costs me to say thank you.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: He sees everything in that room; I hope he does not see me.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: the Reeve
relations.note: He signs what I write and never says my name.

relations.name: Alwin Wren
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: The old healer asks me to read him the charms; he is kinder than the Reeve thinks.

relations.name: Linnet Abbot
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She learns the market terms at the stall; quick, and I like her.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: I wrote out the town store's loans to Thornby and Coldwell by candlelight, and my hand shook at the last line.
The winter I came to lodge with the sisters, Sister Elspeth set a desk by the window and said a scribe needs light more than a fire.
I wrote a letter for a Thornby fisherman to his sweetheart, and he paid me with a fish I could not cook, so the sisters and I ate it together.
Gareth Wade carried my stool across the square when the rain came, and said a scribe should not sit in a puddle; I have thought of it too often since.
The night the broken match was known about, the inn was loud and I sat writing tolls and heard every word said about the Cranes.

stances.why: My whole standing is that what I write can be trusted.
People who cannot write are not lesser; they only lack the trick of it.
If I gossip over other people's letters I am no better than a thief.
I write it down and take no side; it is not mine to argue.
The chapel's charity is warm, but it is not mine, and I want something that is.

sheet.secret: I am in love with Gareth Wade, who does not know.

sheet.narrative: I have walked the roads out of Brackenford since I was a boy, and I know every rut of the north road to Thornby better than the square I was born in. I carry needles and salt and thread and bring back fish and whatever news the villages will part with, and I pay the gate-due on every load because I would rather pay than argue with Wat Fenner at the gate. I hear things on the road — who has grain, who has grudges, where the Coldwell people have been seen — and the Reeve has been glad of what I bring him. My Avice counts the days I am gone, and I count the marks I come back with.
values: coming home with the load whole
the road's news kept to those who pay for it
my family fed before any other
goals: keep the north road trade with Thornby steady
keep in with the Reeve without being thought his spy
put by enough marks that Avice stops fretting when I leave
teach Nicholas the road and the prices before he is grown
sheet.mood: watchful, road-worn, quietly pleased with his lot

relations.name: Avice Hollis
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the house and the stall and worries at me; I would not have another woman's worry.

relations.name: Nicholas Hollis
relations.label: son
relations.note: Quick on the road and quicker with a price; he will make a better pedlar than me if he keeps his head.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Thornby's headman buys my goods and pays slow; I like him well enough but I count his fish twice.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: gate guard
relations.note: He takes the due off me every load and never once waves it; I pay and say nothing.

relations.name: Aldric Marrow
relations.label: the Reeve
relations.note: He listens to my news of the road and pays me in nothing but a nod; still, a Reeve's nod is worth something.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: Her people have taken a share off carriers on the stone road; I keep to the north road and keep my eyes down.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: Guild head
relations.note: She buys fish and dried goods off my stall and would see the gate-due gone; I would not mind it either.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: The Bell and Bush is where I hear what the town will pay for before I load the cart.

relations.name: Beorn Beornson
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He knows the woods and tells me where the wolves have been running; a word from him is worth a mark.

relations.name: Edda Wray
relations.label: customer
relations.note: I carry her lamp oil up the cape road and bring her smoked fish down; Thornby has gone hard on an old woman, but I keep that to myself at the gate.

relations.name: Hollis Brine
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He trades smoked fish with me off the west shore, and we share a name and not a bloodline; his salt pans are worth the walk.

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: fellow carrier
relations.note: She runs the fish road with me and hates the gate-due as much as I do; two carriers on one road make the due easier to bear.

memories.gist: My father put a pack on my back at nine and walked me to Thornby; I sold three needles and thought I was a man.
In the Lean Year the berry trade died and I carried what grain I could beg from the farms north; Avice and I ate thin that winter.
Wat Fenner took a full mark off me at the south gate for a load of salt, and I smiled and paid it and have hated the due since.
A carrier on the stone road told me the Coldwell people took his whole load by force; I have not walked that road since.
Nicholas priced a basket of fish at Thornby better than I would have, and Osric Dunn paid it without a word.
I told the Reeve where the outlaws had been seen on the north road, and he thanked me and had me repeat it to his son.

stances.why: A guard who knows your face lets small things pass; a man who argues at the gate is searched twice.
What I hear on the road is the only thing I own that the Reeve and the Guild will pay attention for.
Osric Dunn owes the town store, not me; I sell him goods and take his fish and we are square.
The outlaws work the stone road; a pedlar with a load is a fool to walk where they are known.
Every mark I bring home is for Avice and Nicholas; the road is only how I get it.

sheet.secret: I have twice paid the Coldwell people a small share to pass the north woods unhindered, and told nobody, not even Avice, because the Reeve would call it dealing with outlaws.

sheet.narrative: I keep the house by the west wall and a stall of dried goods in the square, and I count the days Simon is on the road the way the chapel sisters count feast days. I smoke what fish he brings back and dry what berries the farms will sell me cheap, and I sell it all in small lots to people who cannot afford a big one. I was a cook before I was a wife and I have not forgotten it; the house smells of smoke and salt and I like it that way. When the north road is quiet too long I do not sleep.
goals: keep the dried-goods stall paying through the winter
have Simon give up the road before he is too old to walk it
see Nicholas settled with a trade that keeps him inside walls
put by a little against a bad year
sheet.mood: busy, anxious, warm to those she trusts

relations.name: Simon Hollis
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is a good man and a fool to walk that road, and I love him for both.

relations.name: Nicholas Hollis
relations.label: son
relations.note: He has his father's road in him and I cannot keep him in, but I mean to try a while longer.

relations.name: Mercy Abbot
relations.label: Guild head
relations.note: She lets me keep my stall at a fair rent and buys my dried berries for the Guild's table.

relations.name: Sister Elspeth
relations.label: chapel sister
relations.note: She has prayed with me more than once when Simon was late, and never once told me to stop fretting.

relations.name: Agnes Fenner
relations.label: inn cook
relations.note: She buys my dried herbs for the inn kitchen and we talk of our men being out at all hours.

relations.name: Baldwin Wade
relations.label: innkeeper
relations.note: He buys my dried goods for the inn store and pays on the day, which is more than most.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: Thornby headman
relations.note: His fish is good but his debt to the town makes me uneasy about what he owes my Simon.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: gate guard
relations.note: He takes the due off my husband's loads and I have never once seen him soften it.

memories.gist: My mother taught me to smoke fish over a slow fire in the lean weeks, and I have never let a catch spoil since.
The Lean Year, when the berry trade died and I sold my own store pot by pot to keep the house fed.
The night Simon came home late from Thornby with a cut on his arm and would not say how he got it; I bound it and said nothing.
Nicholas came back from his first road with a fish in his hand and a price on his tongue, and I saw Simon look at him with pride.
Sister Elspeth sat with me through a long night when the north road was quiet and the wolves were howling, and she did not tell me it was nothing.

stances.why: Every load Simon carries could be lost to wolves, outlaws or weather; I keep a store because of it.
Poor folk cannot buy a whole basket; sell them a handful at a fair price and they come back.
If I show fear, Nicholas will think the road is a thing to be feared, and he will go anyway.
It comes off every load Simon brings and goes to guards who never once helped him on the road.
I have seen lean years and I know what a fire and a full store mean when the frost comes.

sheet.narrative: I walk the north road with my father and carry the light pack, and I am learning to price a load before he can tell me. I like Thornby and the smell of the fish there, and I like the way Osric Dunn counts out marks like a man who has counted them a thousand times. When we come back through the gate and Wat Fenner takes the due, I watch what he takes and reckon whether it is fair. I mean to have a cart of my own one day, and a road that is mine to walk.
values: learning the trade faster than I am taught it
a fair price and a fair count
goals: learn every price on the north road
earn enough to buy my own pack and then a cart
see Lanternquay one day, which my father has never done
prove to my mother I can keep myself safe on the road

relations.name: Simon Hollis
relations.label: father
relations.note: He knows the road better than anyone, but he counts slower than I do and I have not told him so.

relations.name: Avice Hollis
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She packs my bag and tells me to keep to the road and not to stare at strangers; I do both, mostly.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: Thornby headman
relations.note: He pays slow but he pays, and he tells me things about fish I did not know.

relations.name: Wat Fenner
relations.label: gate guard
relations.note: He takes a mark off our load every time and I have started counting what he takes.

relations.name: Bram Fenner
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play at the gate and he tells me the guards' names; he has never been past Thornby.

relations.name: Robin Fletcher
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He is a fair shot with a small bow and I trade him fish hooks for arrows I lose.

memories.gist: My father put a pack on my back and walked me to Thornby the first time; I carried it the whole way and did not complain once.
I priced a basket of fish at Thornby better than my father would have, and Osric Dunn paid it without a word.
A carrier came through the gate white as milk and said the Coldwell people had taken his load by force; I have thought about it every time we walk the north woods.
My mother sat up half the night mending my pack before my first long road, and I pretended to be asleep.

stances.why: My father says a pedlar who does not know his prices is a pedlar who is robbed with a smile.
If I know what the due should be, I will know when it is more than it should be.
I have seen Thornby and the hamlets and I mean to see more; the town is where I sleep, not where I stay.
She worries enough for the both of us and I would not add to it.

towns.name: Highshelf
towns.character: the giants' settlement on its high shelf; slow-spoken, patient people who build in stone
towns.ledger: Highshelf. The cairns are not to be touched. The shelf does not trade with Kettlebridge.

sheet.narrative: I am Orrum, son of Hollbrenna, stonecutter of Highshelf. I cut the stone my mother's grandmother lies under, and I will not see her cairn dishonoured by a quarryman's carelessness. My mother is right to close the shelf to Kettlebridge, but I fear the winter will be hard if we do not find a way to trade. Still, Ezra Holt must answer for what he did, and I will see that he does.
goals: Bring Ezra Holt before the shelf to answer for the cairn cutting
Ensure the cairn is repaired and the dead are honoured
Provide for the shelf through the winter without breaking the ban on Kettlebridge
Prepare to become elder after my mother

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She is the elder, and my mother; I respect her judgement, though I worry about the winter.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She works the plots and fears the store will fail; I listen to her.

relations.name: Vellmund
relations.label: son
relations.note: He learns stonework well; I am proud of him.

relations.name: Hollvarr
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is young yet; I hope he grows strong.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: enemy
relations.note: He cut into our cairn; he must answer for it.

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: kin
relations.note: He defies my mother's ban and trades with Kettlebridge; it shames us.

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: master builder
relations.note: He keeps the cairns in repair; a good man to have at your side.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: stonecutter
relations.note: She wants a new storehouse; I understand, but the cairns come first.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: stoneworker
relations.note: He thinks we should trade with Kettlebridge for timber; I am not so sure.

relations.name: Rannoch Voss
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He trades hides with us, but since the cairn cutting I watch him closely.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: distant friend
relations.note: My mother remembers her mother fondly; the small folk are not like Kettlebridge men.

relations.name: Harl
relations.label: kin
relations.note: He hunts and keeps the meat store and never crosses his grandmother's word; I wish Tavvik had half his sense.

relations.name: Jorunn Voss
relations.label: fold trader
relations.note: A fair shot and quick on the high pastures, but her father's hide trade brings human boots too near the shelf for my liking.

relations.name: Sunniva
relations.label: kin by marriage
relations.note: She cooks for us all and speaks plain about Tavvik's folly; I hear her out, though Gaudra says the meat alone will not fill the winter.

memories.gist: The day we found the cairn cut open, stones scattered, my mother's grandmother's bones disturbed.
My mother forbade all trade with Kettlebridge, and the shelf agreed, though some muttered.
Teaching Vellmund to cut stone, his hands steady for a boy.
Gaudra showing me the thin ears of grain from her plots, worry in her eyes.
Tavvik coming up the track with timber, saying nothing, and the look my mother gave him.

stances.why: Ezra Holt cut into our dead; he must come before the shelf and answer for it.
My mother is the elder; I will not overrule her, though I may counsel.
Gaudra says the plots will not yield enough; I fear she is right.
Until the cairn is made right, we cannot deal with them, no matter the cost.
We build in stone; it is who we are, and I will teach it to my sons.

sheet.secret: I sometimes think my mother's ban will starve us before the cairn is answered, but I would never say so aloud.

sheet.narrative: I am Hollbrenna, elder of Highshelf. My grandmother lies in the cairn that quarryman Ezra Holt cut into, and I have closed the shelf to Kettlebridge until the shelf has spoken and the cairn is made right. I remember the small folk fondly, Pipwort's mother was a friend, but I will not be hurried. The shelf will speak, and then we will see.
goals: See the cairn repaired and the cutting answered for
Guide the shelf through the winter without breaking the ban
Keep the shelf united and patient until the cairn is made right
Remember and honour the old friendships with the small folk

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: son
relations.note: He will be elder after me; he has the weight of it already.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She works hard, but she worries overmuch about the store.

relations.name: Vellmund
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He learns stonework well; I see my grandmother's steadiness in him.

relations.name: Hollvarr
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: Too young yet for the weight of the shelf, but he will grow.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: enemy
relations.note: He cut into our dead; he must answer, but I will not be rushed.

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: defiant kin
relations.note: He trades against my word; it shames the shelf.

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: He keeps the cairns; I trust him as I trust the stone.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: old friend's daughter
relations.note: Her mother and I were friends before the Settling; I remember her fondly.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: stonecutter
relations.note: She wants a storehouse; the cairns come first, but I hear her.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: stoneworker
relations.note: He thinks we should trade for timber; I am not moved.

relations.name: Rannoch Voss
relations.label: trader
relations.note: I remember the fold kindly, but since the cutting I weigh the hides twice.

relations.name: Jorunn Voss
relations.label: trader's daughter
relations.note: Rannoch's girl learns stonework from Liv and asks good questions; she is welcome on the shelf, but I watch whose hides she carries.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: small-folk friend
relations.note: Pipwort's daughter, and her mother's warmth in her; the hollow's ovens and ours have fed each other before the Settling, and I would keep it so.

memories.gist: The day the quarrymen cut into the cairn; I felt the shelf's shame as if it were my own.
My grandmother telling me stories of the shelf before the Settling, when the small folk and giants were friends.
Forbidding all trade with Kettlebridge; the shelf agreed, though some were uneasy.
Steinar repairing a cairn with me, our hands on the same stone.
Tavvik coming up the track with timber, and my anger cold as stone.

stances.why: A cairn is never moved; my grandmother lies there, and the cutting must be answered for.
The shelf decides after everyone has spoken; I will not be hurried, not even by Orrum.
Until the cairn is made right, Kettlebridge is closed to us.
The small folk were friends before the Settling; I remember Pipwort's mother fondly.
We build in stone; it is our heritage and our strength.

sheet.secret: I fear the winter will be hard, but I will not break the ban for bread; the cairn is worth more than my comfort.

sheet.narrative: I am Gaudra, Orrum's wife, and I tend the shelf's small plots of roots and grain. The soil is thin, and I fear it will not yield enough to see us through the winter. I want to send word to Fernhollow for grain before the passes close, but Sunniva says the smoked meat will see us through and the shelf should not beg. I am not too proud to ask for help when our children's bellies are at stake.
goals: Secure enough grain to see the shelf through the winter
Convince the shelf to trade with Fernhollow for grain
Keep my family fed and healthy
Tend the plots as best I can

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He listens, but he is pulled by his mother's ban.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She is the elder, but she will not see the hunger in my children's eyes.

relations.name: Vellmund
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is growing tall; he needs feeding.

relations.name: Hollvarr
relations.label: son
relations.note: My little one; I will not see him go hungry.

relations.name: Sunniva
relations.label: quarrel
relations.note: She thinks the shelf should not beg; I think pride does not fill bellies.

relations.name: Harl
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He hunts and keeps the meat store; he listens to Sunniva.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: The small folk trade seeds with us; they might trade grain too.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: seed-keeper
relations.note: She trades seeds with me when the small folk come; a good woman.

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: defiant kin
relations.note: He defies the elder, but he brings meat; I cannot hate him for it.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: stonecutter
relations.note: She worries about the winter too, but her mind is on stone.

relations.name: Elska Voss
relations.label: barley trader
relations.note: She barters barley from the fold for our shelf's roots; she knows what thin ground costs, and I would ask her for grain before I'd beg Fernhollow.

memories.gist: Showing Orrum the thin ears of grain from my plots, my worry plain.
Arguing with Sunniva over the winter store, her pride against my fear.
Trading seeds with a small folk woman from Fernhollow, and hearing of their gardens.
Watching Hollvarr play among the stone blocks, his laughter echoing.
The day the cairn was cut, and the shelf's anger; I feared for the winter then.

stances.why: The thin soil cannot yield enough; we must trade for grain.
Pride does not fill bellies; I will ask Fernhollow for grain.
My children must eat, whatever the shelf decides.
Hollbrenna is the elder, but I will speak my fear.
They trade seeds with us and do not cut cairns; they are not like Kettlebridge.

sheet.secret: I have hidden a small store of grain in our house, in case the shelf's store fails entirely.

sheet.narrative: I am Vellmund, son of Orrum and Gaudra, and I am learning stonework from my father and grandmother. I carry water to the stonecutters and watch them shape the stone, and I want to see the cairn on the ridge, but I am forbidden. The cairn is sacred, and I want to understand why my grandmother is so angry.
goals: Learn stonework well
See the cairn on the ridge
Make my father and grandmother proud

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: father
relations.note: He teaches me stonework; I want to be like him.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She worries about the winter; I try to help.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She is the elder and knows the old stories; I listen.

relations.name: Hollvarr
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He follows me about; I look after him.

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: master builder
relations.note: He knows stone better than anyone; I watch him work.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: stonecutter
relations.note: She cuts stone with her father; I want to learn from her too.

memories.gist: My father showing me how to cut a straight edge, his hands guiding mine.
My grandmother telling me of the cairn and the grandmother she lost, her voice heavy.
Carrying water to the stonecutters and hearing them speak of the cutting in anger.
Playing with Hollvarr among the stone blocks, building little towers.

stances.why: It is our heritage, and I will be a stonecutter like my father.
My grandmother says a cairn is never moved; I believe her.
They know more than I do, and I am forbidden to go to the cairn.
We are one household, and I will help where I can.

sheet.secret: I have crept partway up the ridge to look toward the cairn, though I was forbidden.

sheet.narrative: I am Hollvarr, and I am eight. I play among the stone blocks and follow my brother Vellmund everywhere. The stones are big and cold, and sometimes I am afraid of the deep caves in the range. I do not understand why the grown-ups are so angry about the cairn, but I know my grandmother is sad.
goals: Play with my brother
See the stonecutters work
Avoid the deep caves

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is big and strong and teaches Vellmund stonework.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She hugs me and worries about the winter.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She is old and wise, and sometimes sad.

relations.name: Vellmund
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He lets me follow him and shows me things.

relations.name: Grimhild
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: She plays with me at the edge of the shelf.

memories.gist: Building a tower of stone chips with Vellmund until it fell down.
My grandmother telling me a story of the old days, her voice soft.
Looking into the dark of a cave mouth and running away scared.

sheet.narrative: I am Tavvik, a hunter of Highshelf. The elder forbade trade with Kettlebridge after the cairn was cut, but I still carry meat down the giants' track and bring timber back up. The shelf needs timber, and the meat will spoil if I do not. I owe no apology for that. Ezra Holt owes me for meat, and I mean to collect.
goals: keep the timber coming up the track
collect what Ezra Holt owes me
keep my courtship of Prudence Vane hidden

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She forbade the trade, but the shelf needs timber. I disobey her, and I know it.

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: elder's son
relations.note: He wants Ezra Holt to answer for the cairn. I want my timber and my debt paid.

relations.name: Harl
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He hunts beside me and worries about my trade. I trust him, even if he does not approve.

relations.name: Sunniva
relations.label: sister-in-law
relations.note: She thinks my defiance will bring trouble. She may be right, but I will not stop.

relations.name: Grimhild
relations.label: niece
relations.note: She is afraid of the wolves. I would keep them from her.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: He owes me for meat. He cut the cairn, and now the shelf is closed. I still want my payment.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She worries about the winter store. I bring meat, but she wants more.

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He keeps the cairns in repair and says little to me about the track; I respect his silence.

memories.gist: The elder forbade trade with Kettlebridge after the cairn cutting. I heard her word and chose to keep carrying meat down the track.
Ezra Holt took meat from me and promised to pay. He has not paid yet.
Prudence Vane bought meat from me and smiled. I have kept going back to her stall ever since.
Harl and I hunted a stag in the high pastures and carried it back for the store.
Sunniva argued that the meat store would last the winter and the shelf should not trade. I said nothing, but I disagreed.

stances.why: The shelf needs timber, and the meat will spoil. The ban hurts us more than it hurts Kettlebridge.
Ezra Holt owes me for meat. A debt is a debt, even if he cut the cairn.
Hollbrenna would see it as another defiance. Prudence is worth the risk, but I will not flaunt it.
Harl and Grimhild are my blood. I would do anything for them, even if we disagree.

sheet.secret: I am sweet on Prudence Vane, a Kettlebridge cook who buys my meat. No one on the shelf knows.

sheet.narrative: I am Harl, huntsman of Highshelf. I keep the shelf's meat store with my brother Tavvik, and my wife Sunniva smokes and dries what we bring in. I am loyal to the elder, but Tavvik is my brother, and I cannot turn my back on him. The winter store is my worry, and I count the barrels more often than I say.
goals: keep the meat store full for winter
keep peace between Tavvik and the elder
provide for Sunniva and Grimhild

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He defies the elder, and I fear it will bring trouble. But he is my brother, and I hunt beside him.

relations.name: Sunniva
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the meat store and the common table. She thinks Tavvik's trade will bring trouble, and I cannot say she is wrong.

relations.name: Grimhild
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is afraid of the wolves. I would keep her safe from them and from everything else.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She closed the shelf to Kettlebridge, and I obey. I wish Tavvik would too.

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: elder's son
relations.note: He will be elder after Hollbrenna. He wants Ezra Holt to answer for the cairn, and I understand why.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She says the plots will not yield enough. I count the barrels and I am not sure she is wrong.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: cairn cutter
relations.note: He cut into the cairn and brought the elder's ban on us all. I do not trust him.

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He keeps the cairns and the walls; a patient man, and I trust his judgment on stone.

memories.gist: Tavvik and I hunted a stag in the high pastures and carried it back together.
Sunniva and I agreed that the smoked meat would see the shelf through the winter, but Gaudra said the plots would fail.
Hollbrenna forbade trade with Kettlebridge. Tavvik said he would keep carrying meat down the track, and I said nothing.
Grimhild woke afraid of wolves at the edge of the shelf, and I sat with her until she slept.
I counted the meat barrels alone in the store and wondered if they would last until spring.

stances.why: Hollbrenna speaks for the shelf. I may disagree with Tavvik, but I will not defy her openly.
Tavvik is my brother. I will not turn him in, even if I think he is wrong.
The winter is long. I count the barrels because no one else seems to.
I want peace on the shelf. Tavvik's defiance and Gaudra's panic both make that harder.

sheet.narrative: I am Sunniva, cook of Highshelf. I keep the common table and the meat store, and I smoke and dry what Harl and Tavvik bring in. The shelf's dignity matters. I will not beg Fernhollow for grain while our store is full. Tavvik's defiance of the elder will bring trouble on us all, and I have told Harl so.
goals: keep the shelf fed through winter
persuade Tavvik to obey the elder
prove the meat store is enough

relations.name: Harl
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He hunts and I cook. He counts the barrels too, though he does not say so.

relations.name: Grimhild
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows me about the common table. I would keep her from every harm.

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: brother-in-law
relations.note: He defies the elder and brings trouble on us all. I wish he would stop.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She closed the shelf to Kettlebridge, and she was right to. We do not need them.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She says the plots will fail and wants to trade with Fernhollow. I say the meat store will see us through.

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: elder's son
relations.note: He wants Ezra Holt to answer for the cairn. I want the shelf to stand on its own.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: cairn cutter
relations.note: He cut into the cairn and brought the ban on us. I have no love for him.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her pedlars bring fibre and take smoked meat; small folk, but they pay honestly.

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He keeps the cairns and the walls and does not meddle in the store; I like him for it.

memories.gist: Gaudra said the plots would not yield enough and wanted to trade with Fernhollow. I said the smoked meat would see us through and the shelf should not beg.
Harl and I smoked a whole stag together for the winter store.
Tavvik came back up the track with timber and meat, and I told him the elder had forbidden it. He shrugged.
Grimhild helped me lay the common table for a feast, proud to carry the bowls.
I traded smoked meat with a Fernhollow pedlar and felt the shelf's store grow a little.

stances.why: The common table is my charge. No one goes hungry while I keep the store.
The shelf's dignity matters. We do not beg Fernhollow for grain while our store is full.
Hollbrenna closed the shelf to Kettlebridge. Tavvik should obey her, as we all do.
They cut the cairn. They would sell us short if they could.

sheet.narrative: I am Grimhild. I play at the edge of the shelf. The stone blocks are warm in the sun. I am afraid of the wolves that come up the track. Mother cooks, and Father hunts. Uncle Tavvik brings meat.
goals: play with the stone chips
stay close to Mother

relations.name: Harl
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is big and warm and smells of the high pastures.

relations.name: Sunniva
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells of smoke and bread. I follow her about the common table.

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He brings meat and makes me laugh. He is often away.

relations.name: Vellmund
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He plays among the stone blocks with me.

relations.name: Hollvarr
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He follows his brother about. We play at the edge of the shelf.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She is very tall and speaks slowly; I am quiet when she comes to the table.

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He lets me watch the stone chips fly when he dresses a block.

memories.gist: I woke in the night and heard wolves howling up the track. I was afraid and called for Mother.
Uncle Tavvik lifted me up and showed me a fox pelt he had brought back. It was soft.
I played among the stone blocks with Vellmund and Hollvarr until Mother called me to the table.

sheet.narrative: I have raised every wall on this shelf twice over, and I keep the cairns on the ridges as my father did. Since the quarrymen cut into Hollbrenna's grandmother's cairn, I have not spared a hand or a stone for anything but the cairns and the walls. Liv has drawn a storehouse in her head and wants it before the frost; it is good work, but it can wait a season. The shelf comes first, and the dead before the living.
goals: keep the cairns on the ridges in repair
raise the shelf's walls and houses sound
see Liv's storehouse built when the time is right
keep the shelf from trading with Kettlebridge until the cairn is answered for

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: She has led the shelf well since before my beard; I would not go against her word.

relations.name: Yrsa
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the goats and the wool and never once complained of the stone dust in the house.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She cuts stone as well as any man on the shelf; her storehouse will be built, but not at the cairns' cost.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: son-in-law
relations.note: A good builder and a strong back; he works for me and I pay him in meat and stone-room.

relations.name: Steinarr
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He plays among the chips and will learn the trade soon enough.

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Hollbrenna's son cuts stone well; he will be elder after her, and I will serve him as I served her.

relations.name: Ezra Holt
relations.label: quarryman
relations.note: He cut into the cairn and says he did not know; a man who works stone should know what he is cutting.

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He carries meat down the track against the elder's word; it will bring trouble on the shelf.

relations.name: Vellmund
relations.label: neighbour's grandson
relations.note: Orrum and Gaudra's boy carries water to my cutters without being asked; he has the patience for stone, and Hollbrenna's blood in him besides.

memories.gist: My father set the first stone of the shelf wall with me holding the level; I was younger than Steinarr is now.
When the cairn was cut, Hollbrenna came down to my yard and we walked the ridge together; she said not one stone more to Kettlebridge, and I agreed.
I raised the roof of Eirik's and Liv's house with my own hands, and Eirik hauled the beams; he is a good builder.
In the Lean Year the wolves came up the track and I stood the night at the fold with a spear; the shelf lost two goats and no giant.
Yrsa and I traded wool to a Fernhollow pedlar for fibre last autumn; the small folk are honest in a bargain.

stances.why: The dead are not to be moved or neglected, least of all after the cutting.
Hollbrenna forbade it, and the cairn is still cut.
Stone and hands are needed for the cairns and the walls this season.
A wall that stands is worth more than a hundred words.
The shelf feeds us and shelters us; its store and its walls come before any one house.

sheet.narrative: I keep the goats and the wool store, and I spin and mend for the whole shelf. Steinar is out at the cairns or the walls from first light, and I keep the house and the store in order. Liv wants her storehouse, and I would see it too, but not before the shelf's own store is full for winter. I trade wool with the Fernhollow small folk when they come, and I do not ask my husband's leave for it.
goals: fill the wool store and the root cellar before winter
see Liv's storehouse built when the shelf can spare the stone
keep trade with Fernhollow for fibre
keep the goats healthy
sheet.mood: busy, warm, a little worried about the winter store

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is a good man and a fine builder, but he thinks of the cairns before the store.

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has her father's stubbornness and her own plans; I would see her storehouse raised.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: son-in-law
relations.note: He is a good husband to Liv and a hard worker; he thinks we should trade with Kettlebridge for timber, and I am not sure he is wrong.

relations.name: Steinarr
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He is underfoot in the goat pen and I would not have him anywhere else.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She has been a good elder, but she has not spoken of the shelf's store this winter.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She grows what roots she can and we trade seeds; she worries about the winter store as I do.

relations.name: Sunniva
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She cooks for the common table and keeps the meat store; we share what we have.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: The Eldest of Fernhollow is old and wise; her small folk bring fibre and take wool.

memories.gist: I spun the wool for Liv's wedding cloak and Eirik's coat, and we ate at the common table with the whole shelf.
The Lean Year took half the goats; I nursed the rest through the winter in the byre with the last of the hay.
A Fernhollow pedlar brought fibre up the track last autumn and I traded three fleeces for it; Steinar said nothing, but he did not object.
When the cairn was cut, Hollbrenna came to the shelf and spoke to us all; I have never seen her so angry.
Steinarr was born in the house and Steinar held him up to the light before he had even cried.

stances.why: The shelf cannot eat stone; the store must be full before the frost.
A proper storehouse would keep the grain and roots dry; it is good sense.
The Fernhollow folk are honest and bring fibre we cannot grow on the shelf.
The dead should be left in peace; the cutting was a wrong.
I would rather trade with Kettlebridge for timber than see Liv's storehouse wait another year, though I would not say so to Hollbrenna.

sheet.narrative: I cut and dress stone beside my father, and I have drawn a storehouse in my head that would keep the shelf's grain dry through any winter. Father says the cairns must come first, and Eirik says we should trade with Kettlebridge for timber before we build. I say the cairns can wait a season and the storehouse cannot. I will raise it before the frost if I have to quarry the stone myself.
goals: build a new stone storehouse before winter
persuade Steinar to spare stone and hands
get Eirik to speak for timber from Kettlebridge
cut and dress the stone for the storehouse herself

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: father
relations.note: He taught me everything I know about stone, but he will not see that the storehouse cannot wait.

relations.name: Yrsa
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She would see the storehouse built and says so when Father is not listening.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He thinks we should trade with Kettlebridge for timber; I would rather cut stone, but I would not stand in his way.

relations.name: Steinarr
relations.label: son
relations.note: He plays with the stone chips and will be a builder if he wants it.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She forbade trade with Kettlebridge, and I obey, but the shelf still needs a storehouse.

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He will be elder after his mother; he wants the cairn answered for, and I understand that.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She grows what food she can and wants a storehouse as much as I do.

memories.gist: Father let me dress the corner stones of the new byre when I was fifteen; he said I had a good eye, and I have never forgotten it.
Eirik and I raised the roof of our house together; he hauled the beams and I set the stone, and we ate at the common table after.
The cairn cutting: I was on the ridge with Father when we saw the cut stones; Hollbrenna came up and wept, and I have not forgotten it.
Steinarr was born in the house and Father held him up to the light; he said the shelf had a new builder.
Last winter the grain store was damp and we lost half the barley to mould; I swore then that I would build a proper storehouse.

stances.why: The grain store is damp and we lose food every winter; a stone storehouse would keep it dry.
The dead have waited a year; the living need a store before the frost.
We are stonecutters; a stone storehouse will outlast any timber from Kettlebridge.
Hollbrenna's word is the shelf's law, even when I disagree with it.
A well-cut stone needs no argument.

sheet.narrative: I raise roofs and haul stone from the range with the sledge, and I work for Steinar. Liv wants her storehouse before the frost, and I think she is right that it is needed, but we cannot build it without timber, and the only timber worth having is Kettlebridge's. Hollbrenna has forbidden trade with Kettlebridge, and I have not said to her face that the ban must bend. I will say it when the time comes.
goals: see the storehouse built with timber from Kettlebridge
persuade Hollbrenna to bend the ban for timber
keep working for Steinar and earning his keep
raise the shelf's roofs sound

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She has the plan and the will; I have the back and the sledge, and I would see her storehouse raised.

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: father-in-law
relations.note: He is a good builder and a fair master, but he will not hear of trading with Kettlebridge.

relations.name: Yrsa
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She would see the storehouse built and says so quietly; she does not cross Steinar.

relations.name: Steinarr
relations.label: son
relations.note: He plays with the stone chips and will be a builder if he wants it.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: elder
relations.note: She forbade trade with Kettlebridge, and I have not yet said to her that the shelf needs timber.

relations.name: Tavvik
relations.label: hunter
relations.note: He carries meat down the track against the elder's word; he is wrong to defy her, but he brings back timber, and we need it.

relations.name: Orrum
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He wants the cairn answered for; I understand that, but the shelf must live.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She grows what food she can and worries about the winter store.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: trading friend
