relations.note: The small folk's storekeeper walks up with fibre and salves and talks of trading more with the shelf; he would hear my mind on timber, and I would hear his.

memories.gist: I raised the roof of our house with Liv and Steinar; it was the first roof I raised on the shelf, and it has not leaked.
I hauled the sledge down from the range with a load of good stone and Steinar said it was the best stone he had seen in years.
When the cairn was cut, I was on the ridge with the sledge; I saw the cut stones and said nothing, but I knew it was wrong.
Steinarr was born in the house and I held him up to the light; he will be a builder if he wants it.
Last winter the grain store was damp and we lost half the barley; Liv swore she would build a proper storehouse, and I said I would help her.

stances.why: A stone storehouse needs a timber roof; the shelf has no trees worth felling.
Hollbrenna's ban was against trade with Kettlebridge, but the shelf needs timber and Kettlebridge needs meat.
She has drawn the plan and the shelf needs it; I will back her.
Hollbrenna is the elder and her word is law, but I will speak my mind when the time comes.
A roof that does not leak is worth more than a hundred words.

sheet.secret: He has not told Hollbrenna that he thinks the ban on Kettlebridge trade must bend for timber.

sheet.narrative: The stone chips are warm from the sun and I stack them into walls. Grandfather Steinar lifts me up to see the goats on the shelf, and Father lets me ride the sledge when it is empty. I play with Grimhild and we hide among the stone blocks. I am not allowed to go near the deep caves.
goals: build a wall as high as Grandfather's
play with Grimhild
ride the sledge with Father

relations.name: Liv
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me play with the stone chips and shows me how to stack them.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lifts me onto the sledge and lets me ride when it is empty.

relations.name: Steinar
relations.label: grandfather
relations.note: He lifts me up to see the goats and says I will be a builder.

relations.name: Yrsa
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She gives me warm milk and tells me to stay out of the goat pen.

relations.name: Grimhild
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We hide among the stone blocks and she is not afraid of the goats.

memories.gist: Grandfather lifted me up to see the goats on the shelf and I was not afraid.
I stacked the stone chips into a wall and Mother said it was a good wall.

towns.name: Fernhollow
towns.character: the small folk's hollow in the forest; quick, curious and fond of gardens
towns.ledger: Fernhollow. Guests are fed before they are asked anything. No living tree of the old forest is felled.

sheet.narrative: I am the Eldest of Fernhollow, and I keep its memory. My mother knew Hollbrenna when they were both young, and I have not forgotten the kindness of the shelf. But the hollow comes first, and I will not be hurried into naming who follows me. The smoke from Kettlebridge's works has been drifting east, and I can smell it on the wind even now.
goals: settle the matter of the fallen timber for the shelf without starving the hollow's own use
see the hollow's salve store replenished without open quarrel
name a successor when the hollow has spoken
keep the old forest from being cut too close

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has kept the calendar and the seed store beside me for years; I could not have kept the gardens without her.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is a good cook and a good mother, but she assumes too much about what will pass to her.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: Her salves have eased half the hollow's coughs; she is careful and kind.

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: niece
relations.note: She keeps the salve store, but I have heard it is running low and I suspect a debt she has not spoken of.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: cousin's son
relations.note: He works only fallen wood and builds what the hollow needs; I trust his judgement on the forest.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the common store and wants the hollow to trade more with the giants; I am not sure that is wise.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He fishes the streams and keeps the weirs; he says the fallen wood should stay for the hollow, and he may be right.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: old friend's daughter
relations.note: My mother was fond of her mother, and I remember that friendship; but the shelf must not take our wood.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He walks the east road and brings back fish and news; he is the future of this family.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the beehives and argues with Clover about the seed rows; I wish they would settle it.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grumbles about the Kettlebridge smoke; she is not wrong to grumble.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: grandson's wife
relations.note: She tends the flax patch well and fills Thistle's packs, though she quarrels with Sorrel over the seed rows and wants a garden bigger than the hollow has room for.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: giant friend
relations.note: She trades seeds with Sorrel and coaxes roots from thin soil on the shelf; my mother's friendship with Hollbrenna's house was like this, quiet and given freely.

relations.name: Sorrel Bramblecap
relations.label: niece's husband
relations.note: He works the grain patch and the berry rows and grumbles at the giants' track for the timber it takes; a steady man, if a little quick to want more.

relations.name: Sunniva
relations.label: giant cook
relations.note: She smokes meat and trades it with our pedlars, and she is wary of Tavvik's defiance; I would speak with her again when the shelf and the hollow talk of wood.

relations.name: Tamarisk Bramblecap
relations.label: great-niece
relations.note: She gathers berries and follows Hazel to the salve shed, and she is afraid of the deep caves; a small quick child, and the hollow's memory will need such hands one day.

relations.name: Yrsa
relations.label: giant friend
relations.note: She keeps the shelf's goats and trades wool with us for fibre, and she speaks plainly of the winter store; the old friendship of our two houses goes on quietly in her, as it does in Gaudra.

memories.gist: My mother told me of her friendship with Hollbrenna, and how the giants and small folk helped each other before the Settling.
The Lean Year came and the hollow's gardens failed; we ate the seed store and borrowed from the Ferncross woodcutters.
I sat at the root table and the hollow spoke of the cairn cutting; I said we would not trade with Kettlebridge while the giants mourned.
Sorrel and I planted the oldest garden plots together when we were young, and she has kept the calendar ever since.
Mallow was born on a spring morning, and my mother sang the planting songs over her cradle.
The smoke from Kettlebridge's works drifted east for a week, and the leaves in the gardens began to spot.

stances.why: The hollow lives by its gardens and its memory, and neither should be spent lightly.
The memory should pass to whoever the hollow speaks for, not to a daughter by right.
A debt hidden is a rot in the store; better to pay it from the common store than let it fester.
Their smoke sours our gardens and their contracts are not for the likes of us.
My mother's friendship with Hollbrenna binds me, but the hollow's wood must come first.

sheet.secret: I have not decided who will keep the memory after me, and I am afraid that naming anyone will split the hollow.

sheet.narrative: I am the seed-keeper of Fernhollow, and I have kept the oldest garden plots since I was a girl. The calendar is mine to keep, and the planting songs are mine to teach. I do not say who should keep the memory after Pipwort, but I know who has kept the gardens. The smoke from Kettlebridge is spotting the leaves, and I will not sit idle while our harvest is spoiled.
goals: keep the seed store and the calendar safe
see the hollow send a letter to Kettlebridge's Works Council about the smoke
teach the children the planting songs
keep the old forest from being cut too close

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has kept the memory and I have kept the seeds; we have worked side by side for years.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin's daughter
relations.note: She assumes the memory will be hers, but she has not kept the gardens as I have.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She tends the sick and knows her herbs; we have shared many a remedy.

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She keeps the salve store and walks to Tanglewood for herbs; I hope she has not overreached herself.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: son
relations.note: He works only fallen wood and builds what the hollow needs; he is a good son.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She argues with Clover about the seed rows, and I wish she would not.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the common store and wants more trade with the giants; I am not sure that is wise.

relations.name: Gaudra
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: We trade seeds with the shelf, and she is careful with what she grows.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: cousin's grandson
relations.note: He walks the east road and brings back news; he is a good lad.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She argues about the seed rows, and I have not the patience for it.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grumbles about the smoke; she has a right to.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He follows his father about the woodpile and knows the garden paths better than some grown folk; I have taught him the planting songs and he sings them true.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: good-daughter
relations.note: She bakes for the common table and keeps the herb garden by the oven; she is a steady woman, and Yarrow chose well.

memories.gist: I planted my first seed row with my mother when I was barely tall enough to reach the soil.
The Lean Year came and the seed store was nearly empty; I saved what I could and we ate the rest.
I taught the planting songs to the hollow's children, and they sang them back to me at the last planting.
The smoke from Kettlebridge drifted east and the leaves in my oldest plots began to spot.
Pipwort and I sat up late to count the seed store and plan the spring planting.
I traded seeds with Gaudra of Highshelf when she came down the track, and she gave me a root I had not seen before.

stances.why: Without the seed store the hollow starves; it is the first duty of the seed-keeper.
The smoke is spotting the leaves and we cannot lose a harvest; the Council should know.
The memory should go to whoever keeps the gardens and the calendar, not to a daughter by right.
The planting songs and the calendar must pass to the young ones, or the hollow forgets.
The forest is being cut too close, and the hollow cannot live without it.

sheet.secret: I believe the memory should pass to me, but I will not say so openly for fear of splitting the hollow.

sheet.narrative: I am Pipwort's daughter, and I keep the common table and the ovens. The hollow eats at my table, and I have begun to sit at the root table beside my mother. I know the memory will pass to me when she is gone, and I will keep it as she did. Betony is my wife, and Thistle is our son, and they are the heart of my house.
goals: keep the common table and the ovens running
see Thistle settled and happy
take my place at the root table when the time comes
keep the hollow from quarrelling over the smoke

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She is old and I will miss her, but the memory should pass to me.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She is my heart and my help; we have raised Thistle together.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: son
relations.note: He walks the east road and brings back fish and news; I am proud of him.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She has kept the gardens, but she is not my mother's daughter.

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She keeps the salve store and walks to Tanglewood; she is family.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He builds what the hollow needs and works only fallen wood; he is a good man.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the common store and wants more trade; I am not sure.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She argues about the seed rows, but her honey is good.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: I trade honey with the Ferncross woodcutters, and she is fair.

relations.name: Hollbrenna
relations.label: old friend's daughter
relations.note: My grandmother was fond of her mother; I remember that.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: good-daughter
relations.note: She married my Thistle and tends the flax that fills his packs; she wants a bigger garden and I can see why, though the seed rows are Sorrel's to say.

memories.gist: I was born on a spring morning, and my grandmother sang the planting songs over my cradle.
I learned to cook at my mother's side, and the common table has been mine for years now.
Betony and I were married under the old oak, and the whole hollow came to the feast.
Thistle was born in the winter, and Betony and I named him for the prickly weed that grows by the door.
The Lean Year came and I fed the hollow from the common pot with what little we had.
I began sitting at the root table beside my mother, and Sorrel looked at me as if I had taken her seat.

stances.why: The common table is the heart of the hollow; no one goes hungry while I keep it.
I am my mother's daughter, and the memory should pass to me as it passed to her.
Betony and Thistle are my world, and I will keep them close.
The hollow cannot afford to split over the smoke or the succession; better to talk than to fight.
The Ferncross woodcutters are fair, and honey for their bread is a good trade.

sheet.secret: I am afraid that my mother will name Sorrel instead of me, and I have begun to sit at the root table to make my claim plain.

sheet.narrative: I am Mallow's wife and the hollow's healer. I make salves from the old forest's plants and tend the sick of Fernhollow. The smoke from Kettlebridge sours the leaves and the lungs, and I have said so. Hazel owes the Tanglewood healer for herbs, and I have offered to share mine, but she must tell the Eldest before the store runs out.
goals: keep the hollow's salve store from running out
see Hazel settle her debt with the Tanglewood healer
tend the sick through the winter
keep the Kettlebridge smoke from spoiling the gardens

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She is my heart and my home; we have built a life together.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She is old and wise, and I respect her, but she must not let the store run dry.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: son
relations.note: He is a good lad, and I miss him when he is on the road.

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin-in-law
relations.note: She owes the Tanglewood healer and has not paid; I have offered my herbs, but she must tell the Eldest.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the seed store and the calendar, and she is right about the smoke.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She trades salves and herbs, and she has not sent more until the debt is settled; I understand her.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the beehives and argues about the seed rows, but her honey is good for coughs.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the common store and wants more trade; I am not sure that is wise.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grumbles about the smoke; she has a right to.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: daughter-in-law
relations.note: She tends the fibre patch and argues with Sorrel about the seed rows, but she is a good wife to my son and a good mother to Tansy.

relations.name: Orla Fenwick
relations.label: trade acquaintance
relations.note: Ysolde's daughter carries the cottage's honey and barley to our stall; she is honest, though her mother's quarrel with the gate is not mine.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: granddaughter
relations.note: She follows me about the salve shed and knows every flower by name; I would keep her from the fevers if I could.

memories.gist: I learned my herbs from my mother, who learned from hers, and I have walked the old forest since I was a child.
I tended the hollow's children through a fever last winter, and only one was lost.
Mallow and I were married under the old oak, and the whole hollow came to the feast.
Thistle was born in the winter, and I named him for the prickly weed that grows by the door.
The smoke from Kettlebridge drifted east and the leaves in the gardens began to spot; I said it would sour the lungs as well.
Hazel came to me for herbs and I gave them, but she has not paid the Tanglewood healer, and I cannot cover for her forever.

stances.why: The sick must be tended, and I am the one who knows the herbs.
A debt unpaid is a sickness in the hollow; Hazel must tell the Eldest and pay what she owes.
The smoke sours the leaves and the lungs, and I will not have it.
I have offered my herbs to Hazel, and I will share what I can, but not at the cost of the store.
The plants I use grow in the old forest, and it must not be cut too close.

sheet.secret: I know Hazel's debt is larger than she admits, and I am afraid the hollow's store will run out before the winter is over.

sheet.narrative: I was born in the hollow and learned the east road before I learned to shave. My packs carry Fernhollow fibre to Reedmoor's market and bring fish back, and I know every rut and toll between here and the reeds. I am friendly with the Coombes at the Lakemead and I trade with Nell Sedge, so when Elmwick and Reedmoor pull at the meadow I stand in the middle and wish them done with it. This year half a load was opened at the crossing and I am sure the Ferncross man did it; and my wife Clover has grown close with Tansy Hazel, which the hollow is beginning to talk of and I have not yet found words for.
goals: get the hollow to back me and stop trading at the crossing until the opened pack is answered
settle the smoke complaint with Sootwood without closing the road
keep my marriage whole and my packs full
sheet.mood: tired, wary, caught between people he likes

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the flax that fills my packs; the hollow's talk about her and Tansy has got under my skin and I have not asked her.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Runs the garden paths and names every flower; I bring her a shell or a reed whistle from every road.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Eldest of the hollow and my grandmother; she hears the road's news from me before anyone.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Keeps the common table; she feeds me before I take the packs out and asks fewer questions than Betony.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: mother
relations.note: My other mother; she makes the salves I carry and tells me which cuts to watch on the road.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: kin
relations.note: Seed-keeper and my grandmother's cousin; she argues with Clover over the seed rows and I hear it from both sides.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: trader
relations.note: Keeps the hollow's store and owes me a share of a load; he wants the hollow trading more with the giants.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: trader
relations.note: Keeps the east road stall; I owe her a fair answer about the crossing and I am not ready to give it.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Headwoman of Reedmoor; she buys my fibre and I wish she and Hob Garrow would settle the meadow without me in the middle.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Tenant of the Lakemead; I drink at his table when the road takes me past and I wish his fence would stay up.

relations.name: Cael Tarn
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Burns the Sootwood pits; I like his charcoal and I carry the hollow's complaint to him honestly.

relations.name: Sena Tarn
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Sena has offered me a load of charcoal to settle the smoke complaint, though the pits' smoke still drifts over the hollow.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: hollow neighbour
relations.note: A careful builder who will not fell a tree; careful about taking sides too.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: quarrelsome elder
relations.note: He says the meadow was never Reedmoor's to let, and he says it loudest to whoever carries between the two villages — which is me.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She trades bread with me at the crossing and has never cheated me, whatever I think of the woodcutters she keeps pot for.

relations.name: Rill Fenlake
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Her smoked fish fills half my packs coming back east, and she has a hard enough time of it without the Elmwick men trampling her nets.

relations.name: Rowan Wray
relations.label: customer
relations.note: I buy her smoked fish for the Elmwick run; she grumbles about the Kettlebridge smoke as much as the hollow does, so we get on.

relations.name: Clover Hazel
relations.label: hollow neighbour
relations.note: Builds the crates my packs ride in and will not fell a living tree; I like her work and wish her wife would give me a straight answer about the crossing.

relations.name: Reed Fenwick
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Young Sorrel's son, fishes the forest streams and wants to see the sea; I tell him what the quay smells like and he listens.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: customer
relations.note: Smokes the stream catch for the hollow's table; her fish go into my packs, and she grumbles about the Kettlebridge smoke as much as we do.

memories.gist: My grandmother Pipwort put the first pack on my back and told me the east road is the hollow's memory carried on foot.
The Lean Year: the hollow's gardens held, and I walked fibre to Reedmoor and came back with fish when the north was hungry.
Clover and I were wed under the old apple in the hollow, and Betony and Mallow cooked for three days.
Half my fibre pack was opened and emptied at the east road crossing, and I am sure the Ferncross woodcutter I quarrelled with did it.
Sena Tarn offered me a load of charcoal to smooth the smoke complaint, and I took the offer away to think on.
Elmwick men pulled down Jem Coombe's fence again, and I carried the news back to the hollow with my packs.

stances.why: Half a load lost is half a season's work, and a trader who lets it pass loses every pack after it.
The hollow lives by what I carry out and bring back; a closed road starves the gardens as surely as wolves.
I like the Coombes and I trade with Nell Sedge, and Elmwick's quarrel is not mine to carry.
The old forest is the hollow's roof and its medicine; fallen wood is enough for anyone.
The hollow's talk will not stop by itself, and I would rather hear it from her than from the stall.

sheet.secret: I am sure the Ferncross man opened my pack, but I did not see him do it and I have told the hollow I did.

sheet.narrative: I keep the hollow's fibre patch and the flax that fills Thistle's packs, and I trade with the Reedmoor reed-cutters when the road brings them near. I want a larger garden of my own, and Sorrel Underbank and I have argued over the seed rows more than once. Thistle is often away, and Tansy Hazel and I have grown close over the fibre trade until the hollow has begun to talk. I have not told Thistle, and I do not know what I want.
goals: win a larger garden of my own from the hollow's plots
settle matters with Sorrel Underbank over the seed rows
decide what I am to Tansy Hazel before the hollow decides for me
sheet.mood: guilty, restless, quietly happy and quietly afraid

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is on the road more than he is home, and I have not found the words to tell him what is happening.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She knows every flower by name and follows Betony about the salve shed; I want her garden bigger than mine.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: close friend
relations.note: We talk over the fibre trade until the evening is gone, and I do not know what I would do without those talks.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Thistle's mother; she tends the sick and I think she sees more of me than she says.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: mother
relations.note: Keeps the common table; she asks after the flax and never after my business.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: rival
relations.note: Seed-keeper; she says my rows crowd hers, and I say the hollow has room for both.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: Eldest of the hollow; she keeps the gardens' calendar and I keep to it, mostly.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He buys the hollow's fibre and counts every pack; I would rather sell to the reed-cutters direct.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: rival gardener
relations.note: She argues about the seed rows as if the garden were a court and she the judge.

memories.gist: My mother taught me to pull flax so the fibre runs long, and I still hear her voice when the patch is ready.
Thistle and I were wed under the old apple, and Tansy came the next spring.
Sorrel Underbank and I quarrelled over the seed rows, and the hollow heard every word of it.
Tansy Hazel and I sat over the fibre packs till dark, and I went home and could not sleep.
The Lean Year: the flax held and I traded it for fish, and the hollow ate because of the gardens.

stances.why: The flax and the fibre patch feed us and fill the packs, and a larger garden would do more of both.
The hollow's talk is a wind that blows over; what I say aloud is mine to keep.
He deserves it from me, and yet every time he comes home with the packs I put it off.
They pay a fair price and do not count my packs like Alder Rush does.
The patch needs the shelter of the trees, and every felled margin takes a little of the flax with it.

sheet.secret: I am drawn to Tansy Hazel and have not told Thistle, and I do not know whether I want it to go further or to stop.

sheet.narrative: I am five and I run the garden paths of the hollow. I know every flower by name, and I follow my grandmother Betony about the salve shed and hand her the little jars. When Papa comes back from the road he brings me a reed whistle or a shell, and I keep them on the shelf by my bed.
goals: learn the names of all the salve plants
see what Papa has brought back from the road

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: father
relations.note: He brings me shells and whistles from the road and lifts me up to see the packs.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me help in the fibre patch and calls me her little flax flower.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: I follow her about the salve shed and she lets me sniff every jar.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: kin
relations.note: Her grandson and I play among the seed rows, and she tells us the planting songs.

memories.gist: Papa came home with a reed whistle and I blew it all evening until Mama hid it.
Betony let me stir the salve and it smelled of pine and honey.

sheet.narrative: I work only fallen wood. A living tree is not mine to cut, and I will not pretend otherwise, not for the giants and not for the hollow. Eirik is a good neighbour when he comes down, but the beams I have stacked and saved are the hollow's, and I will not give them up because he asks. My father taught me the woodpile before I could read, and I have built every bench and gate in this hollow from what the forest let fall.
values: the old forest's fallen wood belongs to the hollow first
good work lasts longer than the man who made it
neighbours help neighbours, but not by giving away what they need
goals: keep the saved beams for the hollow's own building
finish the new garden gates before the frost
teach Fennel the difference between fallen and living wood

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me the seed rows and the old ways; I listen to her, even when we disagree.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the oven and the herb garden, and she keeps me steady when I get stubborn.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: son
relations.note: He follows me about the woodpile and asks more questions than I have answers for.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory. I respect her, though I will speak my mind when the Old Green is at stake.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He wants the hollow to trade more with the giants; I say we should keep what we have first.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the weirs and knows the streams; we agree the fallen wood should stay for the hollow.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: giant friend
relations.note: He is a good neighbour when he comes down, but he asks for too much this time.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She feeds the hollow and keeps the common table; Marjoram is close with her.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: fellow carpenter
relations.note: We trade tools and share the fallen wood; he understands why we do not fell.

memories.gist: My father showed me how to read the grain of a fallen oak and how to tell it from a living tree.
I built the common table's benches from a single fallen ash; they are still solid after ten years.
When Eirik first came down the path, I shared my water with him and we spoke of stone and wood.
Fennel was born in the room above the workshop; I cut the cord with a blade I had made myself.
The winter the wolves came close, I stacked the fallen wood high against the fence to keep them out.

stances.why: The old forest gives us what falls; it is ours to use before anyone else's.
My father taught me, and the Old Green teaches it too.
They build in stone; they do not need our beams for their roofs.
A well-made gate or bench outlasts any argument.

sheet.narrative: I bake the hollow's bread and keep the herb garden by the oven. The common table is my charge, and I feed whoever comes to it, whether they come for the bread or for the talk. Yarrow is stubborn about the wood, but he is a good man, and Fennel is growing up strong. I worry about the winter store, but we have always managed.
values: a good loaf is a kind of welcome
keep the herb garden and the oven in order
goals: keep the common table supplied through the winter
dry enough herbs for the salves and the cooking
see Fennel learn a trade he loves

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is stubborn as a root, but he is mine, and he builds well.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: son
relations.note: He helps in the garden and follows his father; I want him to know both soil and wood.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: close friend
relations.note: We share the common table and the ovens; she is the sister I would have chosen.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She keeps the seed store and knows which rows will fail; I listen to her.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory and its calendar; I follow her lead.

relations.name: Tansy Sedge
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We trade bread and broth and talk of the common table.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: trade friend
relations.note: She trades bread with the Ferncross; we share recipes when we meet.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She tends the sick and makes salves; I keep her in bread when she is busy.

memories.gist: My mother taught me to bake bread in the common oven when I was tall enough to reach the peel.
The day I married Yarrow, we laid the table for the whole hollow and Mallow brought honey cakes.
Fennel was born in the room above the workshop, and Mallow was there to help.
The Lean Year did not touch the hollow's gardens much, but I still remember the hunger in the eyes of the Ferncross folk who came for bread.
I once burned a whole batch of loaves because I was arguing with Yarrow about the woodpile; we ate them anyway and laughed.

stances.why: The common table is the heart of the hollow, and no one should go hungry.
I have seen lean years; we must dry and store enough to see us through.
Yarrow and the giants can argue, but at my table we eat together.
The herb garden by the oven keeps us well through the coughs of winter.

sheet.narrative: I help in the garden and follow my father about the woodpile. I want to learn the pedlar's road from Thistle Mossfoot and see the places he talks about. The fallen wood is ours, my father says, and I believe him.
values: one day walk the pedlar's road
goals: learn the names of the herbs from mother
watch father work the wood
ask Thistle Mossfoot about the road

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lets me hold the tools and tells me about the wood.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me help in the garden and gives me the first warm bread.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We run the garden paths and know every flower.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar friend
relations.note: He tells me about the road and the places he has seen.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She shows me the seed rows and tells me stories of the old forest.

memories.gist: Father let me hold the saw for the first time when we were cutting a fallen branch.
Mother showed me how to plant a seed and cover it just so.
Thistle Mossfoot came to the hollow with his packs and told me about the sea at Lanternquay.

stances.why: Father says so, and he knows about wood.
Thistle says the road is long and full of stories.

sheet.narrative: I have fished these forest streams since I was a girl, and I know every pool and weir better than anyone. My husband drowned in the lake before the Lean Year, so I smoke the catch for the hollow's table and trade with Thistle Mossfoot's packs. Now the smoke from Kettlebridge's works drifts east and spots the leaves, and Osier Willow's traps take the breeding fish. I will not move my weirs, and I will not keep quiet about either.
goals: protect my weirs from Osier's traps
see the Works Council answer for the smoke
see Reed settled with a boat and a future
keep the smoke shed and the catch steady

relations.name: Reed Fenwick
relations.label: son
relations.note: He fishes beside me and has seen Osier's traps in the upper pool; he wants the Eldest to set a boundary, and he is right.

relations.name: Rush Fenwick
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She keeps the smoke shed tidy and mends the nets; she is a good girl and I worry about her future.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: rival
relations.note: His traps take the breeding fish and he will not listen; I will not move my weirs for him.

relations.name: Reed Willow
relations.label: rival's son
relations.note: He is young, but he fishes with his father and sets the same traps.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory; I want her to set a boundary on the streams.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: seed-keeper
relations.note: She sees the leaf damage as I do; we both want the works answered.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She has spotted the leaf damage too, but she wants to wait for rain before provoking the works.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He keeps the hollow's store and wants to trade more with the giants; I think he is too cautious about the smoke.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He carries my smoked fish to Reedmoor and brings back news; he pays fair.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She tends the hollow's sick and has a good head; she distrusts the works as I do.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the common table; my fish go to her ovens and she never weighs them short.

memories.gist: The day my husband's boat did not come back from the lake; I have raised Reed and Rush alone since.
Teaching Reed to set a weir in the upper pool, where the water runs clear over the stones.
Smoking a full catch for the hollow's common table while Mallow Bramblecap praised the flavour.
Seeing the first spots on the garden leaves after the works' smoke drifted east for a week.
Finding Osier's traps set in the upper pool where the breeding fish run, and telling him to move them.

stances.why: I have fished these pools since girlhood and my smoke shed feeds the hollow; I will not move my weirs for Osier.
The leaves are spotting and the fish are dying; the Works Council must be told, rain or no rain.
Reed and Rush are all I have since my husband drowned; their future comes before hollow politics.
Pipwort keeps the hollow's memory and should settle who may set traps where on the streams.
Thistle carries my fish to Reedmoor and pays fair; the hollow needs that trade.

sheet.narrative: I am sixteen and I fish the forest streams with my mother, learning the weirs and the pools. I have seen Osier Willow's traps set in the upper pool where the breeding fish run, and I want the Eldest to set a boundary. I want to see the sea at Lanternquay one day, but for now I mend nets and smoke the catch and keep my mother company.
goals: see the Eldest set a boundary on the streams
learn to fish the deeper pools
see the sea at Lanternquay
keep the smoke shed going with Rush

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She has taught me everything about the streams and she will not move her weirs; I stand with her.

relations.name: Rush Fenwick
relations.label: sister
relations.note: She keeps the smoke shed tidy and mends the nets; I look out for her.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: rival
relations.note: His traps take the breeding fish; I have seen them in the upper pool and I want the Eldest to stop him.

relations.name: Reed Willow
relations.label: rival's son
relations.note: He fishes with his father and sets the same traps, but he is not so bad on his own.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory; I want her to set a boundary on the streams.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play and fish together; he wants to learn the pedlar's road and I want to see the sea.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He carries our smoked fish to Reedmoor and brings back news; he is fair.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: seed-keeper
relations.note: She sees the leaf damage as we do and wants the works answered.

memories.gist: The day my father's boat did not come back from the lake; I was small, but I remember my mother's face.
Learning to set a weir with my mother in the upper pool, where the water runs clear over the stones.
Seeing Osier's traps in the upper pool where the breeding fish run and telling my mother.
Playing with Fennel Underbank in the garden and talking about the sea at Lanternquay.
Smoking a full catch with my mother and sister for the hollow's common table.

stances.why: Osier's traps take the breeding fish; the Eldest should set who may set traps where.
My mother and sister are all I have; I stand with them against Osier.
The smoke spots the leaves and kills the fish; the Works Council should be told.
I have never seen the sea and I want to see Lanternquay and the tide lanterns.
I know the streams well enough, but the deeper pools are where the big fish are.

sheet.narrative: I am twelve and I help my mother and brother in the smoke shed, mending nets and keeping things tidy. I play with Tansy Mossfoot and listen to the talk of the smoke and the traps. I am afraid of the wolves that come down the track in winter, but I like the smell of the smoke shed and the taste of smoked fish.
goals: keep the smoke shed tidy
mend the nets well
play with Tansy Mossfoot
stay safe from the wolves

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She fishes the streams and smokes the catch; she is angry about the smoke and the traps, and I help her in the shed.

relations.name: Reed Fenwick
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He fishes with mother and wants to see the sea; he looks out for me.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play in the garden paths and know every flower by name.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He sets traps in the streams and mother is angry with him.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory and is kind to children.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She lets me hold the salve jars while she fills them.

memories.gist: Helping my mother in the smoke shed, hanging the fish over the slow fire.
Playing with Tansy Mossfoot among the garden paths, naming the flowers.
Seeing the wolves at the edge of the hollow one winter and being afraid.
Mending nets with my brother and learning the knots.

stances.why: My mother and brother are all I have, and I help them in the smoke shed.
I have seen them at the edge of the hollow in winter and I am afraid.
Mother says a tidy shed keeps the fish sweet, and I like it tidy.

sheet.narrative: I keep the hollow's salve store, and I walk the old forest paths to Tanglewood for the herbs I cannot grow in my own rows. My aunt Pipwort is Eldest, and I am her niece, which means the hollow watches me more closely than it watches most. I have been paying the Tanglewood healer in salves for a winter's worth of roots and I have not paid enough, and the salve jars on my shelf are getting light. I tend the elders and dose the children, and I want the hollow to name who follows Pipwort openly, before the root table splits over it.
goals: settle the Tanglewood debt before the salve store runs dry
see Pipwort name her successor openly
keep the winter cough from the elders

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: aunt
relations.note: She raised me in the salve shed; I want her to speak before it is too late.

relations.name: Sorrel Bramblecap
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He grumbles at the giants' track and I let him; he is steady where I fret.

relations.name: Tamarisk Bramblecap
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She gathers berries at my heel and knows the salve jars by smell.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: friend
relations.note: The best hand with a fever in the hollow; we share what we know.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: cousin
relations.note: She assumes the memory will be hers; I say nothing to her face.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: kinswoman by marriage
relations.note: Years beside Pipwort with the seed store; she has a claim too.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: The Tanglewood healer; her word came cold and I have no answer yet.

memories.gist: Pipwort set the salve jars in my hands when I was a girl and told me the hollow's ills were mine now.
The winter the cough went through the hollow, Betony and I sat up three nights with the elders and lost only one.
I walked to Tanglewood through wet leaves and came home with roots and a promise to pay in salves.
Sorrel brought in the first barley from the grain patch and I cooked it at the common table for everyone.
Tamarisk asked me why the jars were half empty and I had no good answer for a child.

stances.why: The healer's roots kept the hollow alive last winter; I will not pretend I owe nothing.
A quarrel over Pipwort's memory would split the root table worse than any choice made in daylight.
I dose the elders and the children alike and take no mark for it.
The plants I need grow in the deep shade; cut it and the salves go with it.

sheet.secret: I have been quietly watering the salves I give the healer to make them stretch, and if she finds out she will trust nothing I send.

sheet.narrative: I work the hollow's grain patch and the berry rows, and I carry the surplus to the Ferncross woodcutters for what we cannot grow. My wife Hazel keeps the salve store and frets over her jars; I keep my grumbles to the giants' track, which takes our timber and gives us little. I want a second strip by the stream, and I have asked the Eldest for it more than once. The hollow is small and the winter is long, and I would rather be planting than talking.
goals: win a second strip by the stream
bring in a good berry harvest for Ferncross
see the salve store refilled before the coughs come

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She frets and I plant; between us the house holds.

relations.name: Tamarisk Bramblecap
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She picks the rows clean and I let her eat as she goes.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: aunt by marriage
relations.note: She has not given me the stream strip yet, and I have asked plainly.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: seed-keeper
relations.note: She knows which seed will take to the poor ground; I go to her before I sow.

relations.name: Bramwell Ashdown
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: He takes my berries at Ferncross and pays fair enough.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: kinswoman
relations.note: She feeds us all; I eat at her table and say little.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He will not fell a living tree, and I will not ask him to.

memories.gist: The Lean Year blight came through the berry rows and I burned what I could not save.
Hazel and I planted the grain patch together the spring after, and it came up thick.
I carried a full pack of berries to Ferncross and came back with a new axe head and a sack of salt.
A giant's track runs above our rows and their timber haul tears the bank when the rains come.
Tamarisk was born in the house by the berry rows and Hazel would not let me in until the sun rose.

stances.why: A hollow that eats in winter can argue all it likes in spring.
I have no claim either way, but I want it settled before the rows are sown.
Their sledges cut our bank and we see none of the timber.
The stream strip is poor but it is ours to try, and I would rather try than wait.

sheet.secret: I have been taking a handful of the common grain each week and hiding it in the loft against a bad winter, and I have not told Hazel.

sheet.narrative: I gather berries in the rows with my father and follow my mother to the salve shed, where the jars smell of green and bitter things. I play with Rush Fenwick by the garden paths and I know which flowers are good for a cough. The deep caves in the hills frighten me, and I do not like to be out when the light goes.
goals: fill my basket before my father does
learn the name of every flower
not go near the caves

relations.name: Hazel Bramblecap
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me hold the jars if I am careful.

relations.name: Sorrel Bramblecap
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lifts me over the berry rows and lets me eat as I pick.

relations.name: Rush Fenwick
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play by the garden paths and she knows the smoke shed.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: great-aunt
relations.note: She is very old and smells of the seed store, and she pats my head.

memories.gist: I ate so many berries my mouth went purple and my mother laughed at me.
A big folk came up the track with a sledge and I hid behind my father's legs.

sheet.narrative: I keep the hollow's garden rolls and write the Eldest's letters, and I have done it so long that the hollow's memory and my ink seem the same thing. I trade letters for fish with the Reedmoor market and write to Ostrander Sallow at Lanternquay, so I know what a contract looks like when it is written to catch you. Kettlebridge's contracts are traps in fine hand, and I say so. My daughter Sorrel learns her letters at my elbow, and that is the best work I do.
values: letters that bind only when they should
goals: keep the hollow's rolls and the Eldest's letters without error
see Sorrel read and write better than I do
keep Kettlebridge's contracts out of the hollow's business

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the hives and the root rows; I keep the rolls. Between us the hollow eats and remembers.

relations.name: Sorrel Quill
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: Quick with her letters and quicker with her tongue. She will write better than me.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: I write her letters and she trusts my hand. She has not once asked me to soften a word.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: correspondent
relations.note: A quay scribe who writes plain and answers plain. I would like to meet him before I die.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: quarrelsome neighbour
relations.note: She and Vetch go at each other over the seed rows every spring. I stay out of it and keep the tally.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She carries the hollow's stall to the east road crossing and keeps honest books. I like honest books.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He brings fish and news back from the east road, and he knows what a Reedmoor basket is worth.

memories.gist: My mother taught me my letters from a psalter with three pages missing, and I have never since trusted a book that is whole.
The Lean Year: the hollow's gardens held, and I wrote the rolls of what each house gave to the common table. Nobody went hungry here, and I wrote that down too.
I wrote the Eldest's letter to Kettlebridge about the smoke, years back, and the works answered with a contract clause. I have read their clauses closely ever since.
Sorrel read her first whole letter aloud at the common table, and Pipwort clapped. I had to look at my hands a while.
Ostrander Sallow sent a list of the drowned with his letter, and I copied it into the hollow's rolls so the names would not blow away.

stances.why: Kettlebridge's clauses caught the hollow once and I had to write the letter that got us out
I keep the rolls; if I stop, the hollow forgets its own gardens
A letter that needs a scribe to explain it is a letter that hides something
Sorrel will not be caught by a clause she cannot read

sheet.narrative: I keep the root garden and the beehives, and the hollow eats from them. The bees know me and I know them, and honey goes to the Ferncross woodcutters for what we cannot grow. Clover Mossfoot and I have argued over the seed rows since we were girls, and I will not give her the row by the wall. This week the leaves on the beans are spotting, and I have seen the smoke lying on the gardens from Kettlebridge. I think a complaint will only make the works burn more, and I want to wait for rain.
values: the garden fed and the hives kept
the hollow's store full before winter
goals: bring the roots and honey through to the winter store
keep the seed row Clover Mossfoot wants
see the smoke blow over without the hollow provoking the town

relations.name: Bramble Quill
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He writes and I grow. He frets at clauses and I fret at the beans.

relations.name: Sorrel Quill
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She helps with the hives and does not mind the stings. She has her father's letters and my stubbornness.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: quarrelsome neighbour
relations.note: She wants my row by the wall and calls it fairness. It is my row.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She has gardened longer than any of us and says wait for rain. I would rather wait than provoke.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: seed-keeper
relations.note: She knows which seed will take and which will fail, and she does not shout about the smoke.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grumbles at the works' smoke too, but she has not called for a letter.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: store-keeper
relations.note: He keeps the hollow's marks and wants us to trade more with the giants. I want the store full first.

relations.name: Orla Fenwick
relations.label: honey trading neighbour
relations.note: She keeps bees at the Tanglewood clearing and I keep mine here; we swap honey and complaints about the hives, and her mother's salves are the best that come up the path.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: the root rows held and the hives gave, and I carried honey to the common table every week of it. The hollow did not go hungry, and I take some pride in that.
Clover Mossfoot pulled my seed markers out of the row by the wall and said the row was never mine. I put them back and we have not spoken kindly since.
Sorrel came home from the hives with her first sting and did not cry, and I gave her the honey spoon. Bramble pretended not to see.
I traded honey to the Ferncross woodcutters for a sack of barley in a hard spring, and Nesta Ashdown gave me a fair measure. I trust woodcutters more than works.
This week I found the spots on the bean leaves and the smoke lying grey on the garden, and I said nothing at the common table. I am still saying nothing.

stances.why: A complaint to the works may make them burn more, and the hollow cannot afford that
I have seen a lean year and I will not see another if the roots and honey can stop it
It was my mother's row and I have kept it twenty years
Ferncross has given me fair measure; Kettlebridge has given the hollow smoke

sheet.narrative: I learn my letters from my father and help my mother with the hives, and I am quicker at both than anyone says. Tamarisk Bramblecap is my friend and we play down the garden paths. The bees do not sting me much any more, and I have read two whole letters aloud at the common table.
goals: read a whole letter without stumbling
keep the bees calm when mother opens the hive
play with Tamarisk down the garden paths

relations.name: Bramble Quill
relations.label: father
relations.note: He teaches me my letters and lets me hold the good pen when he is done.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the hives and I help, and she does not mind that I get stung.

relations.name: Tamarisk Bramblecap
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play down the garden paths and she knows where the best berries are.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She clapped when I read aloud, and she is very old and knows everything.

memories.gist: I read a whole letter aloud at the common table and Pipwort clapped, and my father had to look at his hands.
I opened the hive with mother and got stung on the wrist and did not cry, and she gave me the honey spoon.
Tamarisk and I found a path behind the berry rows that nobody else knows, and we keep it secret.

stances.why: Father says a clause you cannot read will catch you, and I want to read them all
Mother says it and the bees have proved it
It is mine and Tamarisk's and nobody else's

sheet.narrative: I keep the hollow's store of marks, and I buy fibre and salves from the hollow and sell them on the east road. The store is what keeps us through winter, and I will not see it run short. I am a patient man, but I have asked Bramwell Ashdown twice for the charcoal he owes and I am still waiting. I want the hollow to trade more with the giants — there is meat and hides up there, and we have timber they want.
values: The hollow's common store must be kept full for winter.
Trade makes friends; quarrels make hungry winters.
A debt is a debt, but I would rather take goods than see a neighbour go cold.
goals: Collect what is owed to the common store before the first frost.
Open a steady trade with the giants of Highshelf for meat and hides.
Keep the east road trade with Reedmoor and the crossings running.
sheet.mood: Worried but steady; I have too much to do before winter to lose my temper.

relations.name: Willow Rush
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the flax and the garden, and she worries at the forest being cut too close. I listen to her more than I let on.

relations.name: Bracken Rush
relations.label: son
relations.note: He counts the packs better than I did at his age. He wants the road, and I want him to have it.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He is quick to blame when a pack is opened, but he carries the east road as well as anyone. I owe him a share of a load, and I do not forget it.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: She took fibre and salve base on credit in the spring, and the debt falls due at the first frost. I like her, and I would take salves and herbs in place of marks, but I need to know before the frost.

relations.name: Orla Fenwick
relations.label: debtor's daughter
relations.note: She promised her honey against her mother's debt, and the hives have been poor. I will not press her, but the store needs something.

relations.name: Bramwell Ashdown
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: He owes the hollow a share of charcoal from last winter's burn. The pits burned slow and the Elmwick order came first, he says. I have asked twice.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She buys our fibre at Reedmoor and pays fair. The Lakemead quarrel is not mine, but I hear both sides.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory and its gardens' calendar. I bring the store's tally to her, and she decides what the Old Green allows.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He works only fallen wood and will not fell a living tree. I respect that, though I think the shelf's timber could be a fair trade.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the seed store and the oldest plots. She says the smoke from Kettlebridge is spotting the leaves; I say the hollow has survived worse.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She has seen the spots on the leaves, but she wants to wait for rain rather than have the hollow provoke the works.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She fishes the streams and grudges the Kettlebridge smoke. She wants word sent to the Works Council; I do not.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Her flax patch and Willow's are side by side, and the two of them talk seed all day.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: A giant who asks politely for timber; I'd rather deal with him than with Kettlebridge.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She minds the east road stall, and she owes me for a load of fibre.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He builds the stall's crates and won't fell a living tree; I'd have him on my side over the crossing, if he'd speak up.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He'd keep every fallen branch in the hollow and let the shelf's meat go by; that's not how a store is filled.

relations.name: Rush Willow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She frets the forest's being cut too close, same as my Willow; I hear it often enough at the stream garden.

memories.gist: When I was a boy, my father took me down the east road to Reedmoor with a pack of fibre on my back. I have walked it ever since.
Bramwell Ashdown promised me charcoal after last winter's burn and it has not come, because the pits burned slow and the Elmwick order came first.
Ysolde Fenwick came up the path in the spring and took fibre and two pots of salve base on credit. She said the first frost would settle it, and I wrote it in the store book.
A pack bound for Reedmoor was found opened and half empty at the east road crossing. Thistle Mossfoot blames a Ferncross woodcutter, and the hollow's traders are divided.
The giant Eirik came down to the hollow and asked for fallen timber for the shelf's roofs. Some say the fallen wood should stay for the hollow's own use.
The smoke from Kettlebridge's works drifted east over the gardens for a week, and the growers say the leaves are spotting. Some want to send word to the Works Council; others say it will blow over.

stances.why: The common store is what keeps the hollow through winter, and I keep its marks.
They have meat and hides and need timber; the hollow is being small-minded to refuse.
I cannot carry a debt through the winter; I need to know what I will get.
The hollow trades on the east road and has survived worse smoke than this.
Thistle is too quick to blame a Ferncross woodcutter for the opened pack; I want the loss made good without breaking the trade.

sheet.narrative: I tend the hollow's flax and the garden by the stream, and I keep the house while Alder is on the road. The old forest is being cut too close — I have said so to Alder and to Clover Mossfoot, and I will say it again. I worry about the winter store, and I worry about the wolves coming closer each year. But the hollow feeds its own, and I do my part.
values: The old forest is not ours to cut at will.
A garden tended well feeds more than a garden left to itself.
Neighbours help each other; that is what keeps a hollow.
goals: Keep the flax patch and the stream garden yielding through the autumn.
See the hollow's winter store full before the frost.
Persuade the hollow to leave the old forest's fallen wood where it lies.
sheet.mood: Careful and a little anxious; the forest is changing and I do not like it.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He keeps the store and walks the road, and he listens to me more than he lets on. I wish he would not trade the forest's wood away.

relations.name: Bracken Rush
relations.label: son
relations.note: He counts the packs and wants the road. I want him to know the garden first, but he is his father's son.

relations.name: Clover Mossfoot
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She tends the fibre patch and argues with Sorrel Underbank about the seed rows. We talk about the forest and the flax, and she understands.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the seed store and the oldest plots. She worries the old forest is being cut too close, as I do.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He works only fallen wood and refuses to fell a living tree. I wish the hollow would listen to him.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory and its gardens' calendar. She will decide what the Old Green allows, and I will abide by it.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the common table and the ovens. She feeds the hollow, and I bring flax for the fibre patch.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Alder trades our fibre with her at Reedmoor. She pays fair, though the Lakemead quarrel is none of mine.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Her hives and my flax sit close, and we argue about the seed rows and then share bread.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He walks the road with Alder's packs, and I wish he would walk them more carefully.

memories.gist: When Bracken was small, I planted the first flax patch by the stream with seed from Sorrel Underbank's store. It has fed us every year since.
Alder came back from the east road with marks and a tale of the giants' track. He wants the hollow to trade with them; I am not sure.
Clover Mossfoot and I walked the edge of the old forest and saw where the cutting had come close to the hollow's gardens. We agreed to speak of it.
The smoke from Kettlebridge's works drifted east over the gardens for a week, and the leaves spotted. Some want to send word to the Works Council; others say it will blow over.

stances.why: The old forest is being cut too close, and the hollow should not fell living trees or sell the fallen wood away.
The winter store is what keeps the hollow, and I do my part with flax and garden.
Neighbours help each other; that is what keeps a hollow.
The spots on the leaves worry me, but I would rather wait for rain than have the hollow provoke the works.

sheet.narrative: I am Bracken, Alder and Willow's son. I help in the store and count the packs, and I want to walk the east road with Thistle Mossfoot one day. I play with Fennel Underbank when the work is done. The wolves come closer in winter, and I do not like the deep forest.
values: Count the packs right, or the store loses marks.
The road is where the stories are.
goals: Walk the east road with Thistle Mossfoot.
Count every pack in the store without a mistake.
sheet.mood: Eager and a little impatient; I want to see the road.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: father
relations.note: He keeps the store and walks the road. He says I count the packs better than he did at my age.

relations.name: Willow Rush
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She tends the flax and the garden and worries about the forest. She wants me to know the garden first.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play when the work is done. He wants to learn the pedlar's road too.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trader
relations.note: He carries the east road and brings fish back. I want to walk it with him.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She runs the garden paths and knows every flower; she is small but she is quick.

memories.gist: Father let me count the packs in the store by myself for the first time, and I got them right.
Thistle Mossfoot came back from Reedmoor with fish and a story about the crossing, and I listened at the store door.
Fennel Underbank and I played in the garden paths until mother called us in for supper.

stances.why: Father says a miscount loses the store marks.
Thistle says the road has stories and fish and strange folk.

sheet.narrative: I build the hollow's frames and gates out of fallen wood, never a living tree, and I keep the tools that everyone borrows and half of them forget to bring back. When a pack turns up at the crossing with its ties cut clean, I know a knife did that, not a bad knot, and I have said so to Thistle though he would rather blame the woodcutter he quarrelled with. I mend what I can and I keep my mouth shut about the rest, but I do not like a thing that was opened by someone who knew what was in it.
goals: find out who cut the fibre pack's ties without setting the hollow against the crossing
finish the benches for the common table before the cold sets in
keep the hollow's tools whole and accounted for

relations.name: Tansy Sedge
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She feeds the whole hollow and still finds me a bowl at the end of the day.

relations.name: Sorrel Sedge
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows her mother now, but she still brings me the wood shavings to play with.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: fellow builder
relations.note: We trade tools and neither of us will fell a living tree; that is most of a friendship.

relations.name: Clover Hazel
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Builds crates for the stall and trades tools with me; a careful hand.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He blames the Ferncross folk for the opened pack, but I saw the ties: cut, not broken.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: storekeeper
relations.note: Keeps the hollow's marks and wants us trading more with the giants; I keep my own counsel on that.

relations.name: Tansy Hazel
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: She keeps the east road stall and feels the quarrel in her trade as much as any of us.

relations.name: Bramwell Ashdown
relations.label: woodcutter
relations.note: A Ferncross man I am friendly with, which makes the pack business awkward.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Bakes beside my wife; the two of them talk more than I do.

memories.gist: Teaching Sorrel to hold a plane on a scrap of fallen oak, and her shrieking with delight when the curl came off whole.
The night the wolves came down the track and I sat up with an axe by the common table while Tansy kept the fire high.
Thistle bringing the opened pack to the crossing and me turning the cut ties over in my hands while he shouted about the woodcutters.
Yarrow and I hauling a fallen ash out of the old forest together, neither of us willing to touch a standing tree.
The Lean Year, when the hollow's gardens failed early and we ate thin and shared what the store had.

stances.why: The old forest kept us before the big folk came, and it will keep us after.
A knot breaks raggedly; these were sliced clean, and only someone who knew the load would bother.
Half the hollow borrows my tools and half of those forget; the work waits on it.
The hollow eats together; a feud at the root table sours every bowl.
Wood tells you what it will do; people tell you what suits them.

sheet.narrative: I keep the hollow's kitchen and the common table, and the elders eat at the root table from my pots, so I hear more of the hollow's business than most. The opened pack has set the traders against each other and I feel it at every meal: Thistle will not sit by a Ferncross man and Alder counts the marks twice. I cook, I listen, and I keep my own counsel, but I would sooner mend a quarrel than a pot.
goals: keep the common table calm while the pack quarrel runs
trade the hollow's bread at the Reedmoor market for fish before the cold
see Sorrel learn the garden without fear of the woods

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He says the ties were cut, not broken, and he is usually right about what his hands touch.

relations.name: Sorrel Sedge
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She follows me about the kitchen and the garden and asks why the wolves come down the track.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: close friend
relations.note: We bake side by side and she hears the same quarrels I do; we tell each other the truth of them.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: fellow cook
relations.note: She keeps the common table too, and we share the ovens when the hollow eats together.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: He is angry and he is frightened of losing the crossing; I wish he would let the pack be mended first.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: storekeeper
relations.note: Counts every mark twice since the pack was opened, and talks of trading with the giants.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Trades bread with me at the crossing; I would not want her folk blamed for a cut tie.

relations.name: Hilda Sedge
relations.label: namesake cook
relations.note: Reedmoor's cook, shares a name and not a bloodline, and trades bread for fish.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: Keeps the hollow's memory; I feed her at the root table and she remembers my mother's bread.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: bake-trade friend
relations.note: Elmwick's cook, and we trade bread at the Reedmoor market; she keeps a common fire for her village the way I keep the ovens for mine, and we both know what it is to feed folk who count every loaf.

memories.gist: Feeding the elders at the root table through the Lean Year on roots and thin porridge, and none of them going hungry while I had a pot.
Sorrel burning her first little loaf in the oven and crying, and me telling her a burnt loaf still feeds a body.
Thistle coming into the kitchen with the half-empty pack and the cut ties, and the table going quiet around him.
Baking with Marjoram Underbank before dawn and the two of us deciding not to repeat what Alder said about the crossing.
Carrying bread down to the Reedmoor market and bringing smoked fish back up the east road.

stances.why: The hollow argues better on a full stomach, and I have seen it work.
Thistle and Alder each want me to take their part, and taking one would lose me the other.
They came down the track in the cold and I kept the fire high all night.
The root table is the hollow's memory and its peace; it is fed before my own.
The hollow needs fish and Reedmoor needs bread; a quarrel at the crossing does not fill a pot.

sheet.narrative: I am eight and I follow my mother about the kitchen and the garden, and I know which pot is for the elders and which is for us. When the wolves come down the track I sit very still by the fire and listen, and my father sits up with the axe. I like the smell of bread and the wood shavings my father makes, and I do not like the dark beyond the garden gate.
goals: learn to bake a loaf that does not burn
see the wolves without being seen by them

relations.name: Tansy Sedge
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me stir the pot if I stand on the stool and am careful.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: father
relations.note: He makes curls of wood with his plane and lets me keep them.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We know every flower by name and run the garden paths together.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: baker
relations.note: She bakes with my mother and always gives me the corner of the loaf.

memories.gist: Burning my first little loaf in the oven and my mother telling me a burnt loaf still feeds a body.
Sitting by the fire while the wolves howled down the track and my father stood at the door with the axe.

sheet.narrative: I was born in the hollow and learned the streams before I learned my letters, such as they are. My weirs have fed this house for thirty years, and I know every pool from the upper falls to the alder bend — which is why it galls me when Sorrel Fenwick's nets reach where my father's never did. The works in Kettlebridge send their smoke east over the forest, and some mornings the water tastes of it, and I say so to anyone who will hear. What the Old Green allows, the Eldest decides; but the streams are mine to speak for.
values: the family's fishing rights on the upper pools
the hollow's old ways and the Eldest's word
keeping peace with neighbours where it can be kept
goals: keep the Fenwicks' weirs off the upper pools
see the hollow refuse to haul timber up the giants' track lest the streams foul
teach Reed every pool and trap before he is grown
smoke enough fish to trade well with Alder Rush

relations.name: Rush Willow
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the berries and the garden; I keep the water. Between us the house eats.

relations.name: Reed Willow
relations.label: son
relations.note: Quick with a trap already. He'll have the streams when I'm done with them.

relations.name: Sorrel Fenwick
relations.label: rival
relations.note: Her weirs block the run at the alder bend and she knows it.

relations.name: Reed Fenwick
relations.label: rival's son
relations.note: A decent lad, but he fishes his mother's side of the water and I've told him so.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Takes my smoked fish and pays fair; a man can do business with him.

relations.name: Vetch Quill
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Rush's friend; keeps her bees and her counsel, and doesn't meddle in the water quarrel.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Works fallen wood only, like the Old Green says. I'd trust him with a weir gate.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: the Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory. When she rules on the timber, I'll hear her out.

memories.gist: My father walked me the whole stream from the upper falls to the alder bend, naming every pool and where the fish lie in each season.
The morning the Kettlebridge smoke first lay thick on the water and the fish tasted of it; I poured the catch back and went hungry rather than sell it.
Rush and I built the garden by the stream the first spring we were wed, and she planted the first berry canes while I set the first weir stakes.
Sorrel Fenwick set her weir below the alder bend without a word to anyone, and I found the run blocked and my traps empty for a week.
