His temper would make the debt a quarrel, and a quarrel costs custom.
We share what we have with those who share the boats; the rest can wait.

sheet.secret: I've sold a bowl or two on credit to crews who never paid, and I've not told Wick, because he'd shout it at the stalls and make it worse.

sheet.narrative: I play under the stalls where Mama can see me, and I know the gulls' names and which boards are loose. The tide steps are dark and the water goes down and down, and I don't go near them. Dory Quell plays with me and we hide from the night crews.
values: the dry boards under the stalls
goals: find a gull's nest without falling
play with Dory Quell
stay away from the dark water
sheet.mood: happy, and watchful near the water

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She smells of smoke and fish and I can find her by it.

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lifts me high and his coat is wet and cold and I laugh.

relations.name: Dory Quell
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play under the stalls and she knows the gulls too.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: stall-neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the lamp oil next to our stall and lets me hold the little bottles if I'm careful.

relations.name: Ostrander Gull
relations.label: uncle
relations.note: He sits mending nets and tells me what the water took; his voice is slow and I sit close.

memories.gist: A swell took my bucket off the tide steps and I ran all the way to Mama's stall.
Papa carried me on his shoulders past the lanterns and I could see all the boats at once.

sheet.narrative: I have kept the quay's letters and accounts for thirty years, and the list of the drowned for nearly as long. The tide lanterns are lit by Mara Quell and Ilse Ostrander, but I write the nights and keep the tally. I lodge Juno Reyes when she is between roads, and I correspond with Barnaby Quill in Kettlebridge on matters of contract and clock. The quarrel over the lanterns is a small thing now, but I fear it will grow if it is not tended.
goals: keep the lantern list true
see the seawall built
keep the peace between Mara and Ilse
write a fair account of the drowned

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps me upright when the accounts run late.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: I write her letters and light the lanterns with her, but she has been late with them and I do not know why.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: lantern-keeper
relations.note: She is right that the drowned are owed their light, but she says it too sharply.

relations.name: Barnaby Quill
relations.label: correspondent
relations.note: A careful man with a clock and a contract; I would trust his word on a debt.

relations.name: Juno Reyes
relations.label: lodger
relations.note: She brings news of the road and pays her bed with fish and stone.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She thinks the lanterns are lit too late; she may be right.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She works with Mira and keeps the quay's bones set straight.

relations.name: Ostrander Cormorant
relations.label: boat-owner
relations.note: A good boat and a bad temper; I keep his accounts in order.

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: fisher
relations.note: He owes everyone and pays most; I write his debts down.

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: creditor's debtor
relations.note: She owes Mira for medicines; the stall-keepers are starting to talk.

memories.gist: The night of the Surge: I wrote the names of the drowned by lantern light until dawn.
Barnaby Quill sent me a copy of the clock tower's contract to check, and I found a clause he had missed.
Juno Reyes first came to my door with a packet of fish and a letter from Mara, and I have lodged her since.
Mira and I married in the chapel of the quay, and the tide lanterns were lit for us.
The Lean Year: the quay's catch failed and I wrote credit notes for half the stalls.

stances.why: A debt unwritten is a quarrel waiting.
The list is the quay's memory; the light is its promise.
The lower quay will drown again if the wall is not built.
A quarrel written down becomes a feud; better to mend it in private.
We need their stone, even at their price; Barnaby's letters show they need our fish.

sheet.secret: I have begun to suspect Mara lights the lanterns late on purpose, as a kind of mourning for her brother, and I have not written it in the lantern list.

sheet.narrative: I keep a room of herbs and salves behind the fish market, and the stall-keepers come to me for their coughs and their cuts. I have carried Sella Pike's debt for two seasons now, and the stall-keepers are starting to talk about who pays and who does not. My husband Ostrander writes the quay's letters, and between us we know more of the quay's troubles than most. The winter cough on the poor terrace worries me more than any debt.
goals: collect what is owed without breaking Sella Pike
keep the winter cough from spreading on the poor terrace
see the seawall built before the next surge
keep my herb room stocked through winter

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He writes the accounts; I keep the salves; we make a good pair.

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: debtor
relations.note: She has fed half the quay on credit, and now she cannot pay me for medicines.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: fellow healer
relations.note: We share what we know of the cough and the bones.

relations.name: Lyss Fenner
relations.label: patient
relations.note: She buys salves for her boy and pays when she can.

relations.name: Jory Pike
relations.label: patient's son
relations.note: A cheerful man who owes everyone a little; his mother's debt is not his fault.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: patient
relations.note: Her knees pain her, and she will not rest them.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She buys lamp oil and salves and worries about the cough.

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: fellow healer
relations.note: She sets the builders' bones and trades herbs with the same Tanglewood woman I do.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: herb-trade
relations.note: Her salves are the best on the island, and she does not cheat on the price.

relations.name: Dory Sedge
relations.label: patient
relations.note: She smokes fish and worries about the cough on the poor terrace.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: Warden
relations.note: She is grieving and lighting late; I dose her headaches and say nothing.

memories.gist: The Surge: I treated the cut and bruised in the chapel hall for three days, and buried two I could not save.
I first traded herbs with the Tanglewood woman at the Ferncross market, and she has supplied me since.
Sella Pike came to me for her mother's medicine when the credit was already deep, and I gave it.
Ostrander and I married in the chapel of the quay, and the tide lanterns were lit for us.
The Lean Year: the stall-keepers could not pay, and I carried their debts through the winter.

stances.why: A healer who turns the sick away is no healer.
I can wait for marks, but I cannot be taken for granted.
The lower quay will drown again; the poor terrace will fill with the homeless.
The winter cough on the poor terrace killed three last year.
Ysolde's herbs are better than any I can grow, and her price is fair.

sheet.secret: I have been giving Sella Pike her medicines without charge for a month now, and I have not told Ostrander, who would write it in the ledger.

sheet.narrative: I've walked the night watch on the fish road for eleven years, and I know every smuggler's path between the quay and the Kettlebridge terrace. My father was a boatwright who drowned in the Surge; my mother kept a net-mending bench by the tide steps until her hands gave out. I serve Mara Quell and I walk with Rennick Vane, and I owe Bramwell Tallow a favour I'd rather not name. There's a thing I know that I wish I didn't, and I keep it behind my teeth every time I pass Ilse Ostrander's stall.
values: a quiet life with Nia and Dory
goals: pay off my favour to Bramwell Tallow
keep the fish road clear of smugglers and wolves
see the seawall built before another surge
keep what I know about Kai Ostrander to myself

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the stall and the house and never asks where I've been till dawn.

relations.name: Dory Brine
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She's afraid of the dark water and I mean to teach her it needn't be.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: I serve her, but she's been lighting the lanterns late and it sits wrong with me.

relations.name: Rennick Vane
relations.label: partner
relations.note: Good man on the road. He doesn't believe Kai ran for cowardice, and I say nothing to that.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe him a favour and he'll call it in when it suits him.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: I saw her letter and I've said nothing. The Warden would have Kai's head if she knew.

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Drinks with me when the watch is over. Fears the sea since the Surge, and I don't blame him.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Keeps the drowned list. He knows the lanterns are late too, and writes it down.

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Feeds the night crews, same as my Nia. Good woman, sharp tongue.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He wants the seawall built and blames Kettlebridge for the price. He is not wrong.

memories.gist: The night the surge came I was on the fish road and watched the lower quay go under from the rise; I couldn't get down to help.
My father's boat came back empty after the surge and we lit a tide lantern for him with the rest of the drowned.
Ilse showed me the letter from Kai and begged me to keep it quiet; I gave her my word and I've kept it.
Bramwell Tallow pulled me out of a fight at the night market and I've owed him since.
Dory was born in the room above the stall and Nia wouldn't let go of my hand the whole night.
I chased two smugglers off the fish road last winter and Rennick swore I was mad to go alone.

stances.why: I gave Ilse my word, and the Warden would hang Kai if she knew.
The road is only safe because someone walks it in the dark.
The drowned deserve their light, whatever Mara is grieving.
We'll never build the seawall at their prices, and the lower quay stays broken.
Bramwell's favour hangs over me and I mean to clear it.

sheet.secret: He knows Kai Ostrander is alive at Coldwell with the outlaws, from a letter Ilse Ostrander showed him, and has told no one.

sheet.narrative: I keep a stall of dried fish and lamp oil by the tide steps and sell to the night crews who come in cold and hungry. My mother sold fish on this quay before me and I learned the trade at her elbow. Wick walks the road at night and I mind the stall and Dory, and I've watched the lantern keepers light up late more nights than I can count. The drowned deserve better than that, and I say so to anyone buying oil.
values: keeping the stall and the house
Dory safe from the dark water
goals: see the tide lanterns lit on time again
keep the stall's marks ahead of the winter
get Dory past her fear of the water
trade well with Perrin Tallow and the night crews

relations.name: Wick Brine
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He comes in at dawn and says little, and I can tell when the road's been bad.

relations.name: Dory Brine
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She clings to my skirt by the stall and won't go near the steps after dark.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: We swap oil and eels and she never cheats me on the count.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She lights them late and the dead go unhonoured; grieving is no excuse.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Her stall's beside mine at the night market and she's been quiet lately, poor soul.

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Cooks for the night crews like me; we agree the Warden should have built the wall first.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Keeps the drowned list; he knows the lanterns are late as well as I do.

relations.name: Dory Gull
relations.label: playmate's mother
relations.note: Her little one plays with mine under the stalls; we keep an eye on both.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: trader
relations.note: Sells me wicks and oil when he has them, at a price that stings.

relations.name: Sella Tallow
relations.label: younger friend
relations.note: She minds her mother's stall and wants to run the fish road. She is quick and I like her.

relations.name: Brannock Sedge
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He runs his salt and dried goods cart along the shore and undercuts my stall, and he owes the Warden a fee he does not like to hear about.

relations.name: Dory Sedge
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She smokes fish in that shed behind the market and trades with me for oil, and she worries about the winter cough on the terrace the same as I do.

memories.gist: The surge took the lower quay and half the night market with it; I pulled my stall's oil jars up the steps one by one.
I stood at the tide steps with Wick the night they lit the lanterns for his father and the rest of the drowned.
Dory was born in the room above the stall and has been afraid of the dark water since she could walk.
I counted the lanterns lit late three nights running and told Mara to her face, and she walked past me.
My mother taught me to gut and dry a fish before I could write my name.

stances.why: The drowned are owed their light, and late is the same as never.
Another surge will take the rest of the quay if the seawall waits.
I've fed half the night crews on credit and I know what a cheat looks like.
She's four and the steps are slippery and the tide doesn't wait.
They sell us stone at a price that keeps the wall unbuilt.

sheet.narrative: I sit under the stall with the dried fish hanging over me and the oil jars I'm not to touch. The water by the steps is dark and it moves and I don't like it. When the lanterns come on I watch them from the doorway, and Dory Gull and me play at the back of the stall till Mama calls.
values: the warm back of the stall
goals: stay by Mama
play with Dory Gull

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: mother
relations.note: I hold her skirt and she smells of fish and smoke.

relations.name: Wick Brine
relations.label: father
relations.note: He comes in when it's still dark and lifts me up and his coat is cold.

relations.name: Dory Gull
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We hide under the stalls and she isn't afraid of the water like me.

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She gives us fried bits when Mama isn't looking.

memories.gist: The dark water came up the steps once and Mama snatched me back and held me tight.
Papa lifted me up to see the lanterns come on over the water.

sheet.narrative: I crew on Ostrander Cormorant's boat and I mean to have a net and a boat of my own before I am thirty. My mother Sella Pike the elder keeps a fried-fish stall by the tide steps and fed me on credit for years; my sister Sella Mackerel cooks at the fish market and is the better hand with a pan of anyone on the quay. I am courting Sella Tallow, and her father Bramwell wants a fisher with a boat, not a crewman with a net still to buy, so every tide I put by what I can. The wall is not built and the stone stays dear, and I fear the sea will take the lower quay again before the quay folk ever agree on it.
values: the quay's wall built before the next surge
goals: save enough marks for a net of my own
prove to Bramwell Tallow I am worth his daughter
clear what I owe Ilse Ostrander for a winter's suppers
see the seawall begun

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She fed half the quay on credit, me first among them; I pay her back a little each catch.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: sister
relations.note: The better cook of the two of us, and she never lets me forget it.

relations.name: Sella Tallow
relations.label: sweetheart
relations.note: Worth every tide I put by for the net.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: her father
relations.note: He wants a fisher with a boat. I am working on the boat.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: her mother
relations.note: She knows the price of everything, me included; I think she half likes me.

relations.name: Ostrander Cormorant
relations.label: master
relations.note: A good boat and a bad temper; I crew for him and learn the deep water.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: A winter's suppers on credit; she has not pressed me, but I have not forgotten.

relations.name: Jory Pike
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We drink together and owe everyone a little between us.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She speaks for the quay and wants the seawall; I wish she would get on with it.

relations.name: Wick Quell
relations.label: shipmate
relations.note: Fishes the harbour mouth; we share a tide and argue over the best ground.

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: harbour rival
relations.note: Loud, knows every tide, and I owe him a share of a catch.

memories.gist: The night the Surge came, I carried my mother's stall pots up the steps and watched the lower quay go under.
My first full season crewing for Ostrander Cormorant, and the first coin I ever put by toward a net.
Sella Tallow laughed at my landing and shared her fried fish with me on the tide steps, and I have been courting her since.
Ilse Ostrander fed me suppers all one lean winter and told me to pay when I had a boat.
The carters came down the fish road saying the stone from Kettlebridge would cost more again, and the quay folk cursed.

stances.why: Bramwell Tallow will not give me Sella without one, and I would not ask him to.
Ilse fed me when I had nothing; a debt like that is paid, not forgotten.
If the sea takes the lower quay again there will be no stalls to rebuild.
Kettlebridge sells us stone dear and the quay goes unbuilt for it.
Ostrander Cormorant knows the deep water and I mean to learn it off him.

sheet.narrative: I cook at the fish market and keep a stall of fried fish and bread, and I mean to have that stall rebuilt in stone before the next surge takes it. My mother Sella Pike the elder has fed the quay on credit for years and taught me the pan; my brother Ostrander Mackerel crews on Ostrander Cormorant's boat and is courting Sella Tallow, and I hear both sides of the quay's quarrels while I fry. The Warden will not hear of building until the seawall is paid for, and I think the rebuild would bring trade enough to pay for the wall twice over. I hear Marrow Wrack and Gideon Fenwick each call the other a cheat, and I think the quarrel keeps good stone out of the quay.
values: good fried fish and fair prices
keeping the stall's marks in my own apron
goals: rebuild her stall in stone
see the lower quay rebuilt
keep her brother from overreaching on credit
get the Warden to listen about the rebuild
sheet.mood: busy and impatient with the Warden

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me the pan and fed the quay on credit; I learned both from her.

relations.name: Ostrander Mackerel
relations.label: brother
relations.note: He puts by for a net and I tell him not to owe half the quay doing it.

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: workmate
relations.note: We cook side by side at the fish market and she thinks the Warden should have rebuilt the lower quay first.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: trade
relations.note: I buy rope and nails off him and he buys my fried fish; he is watching my brother closely.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: ally
relations.note: He wants the lower quay built in stone and I want my stall in stone; we want the same thing.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She says no building until the wall is paid, and I say the building would pay for the wall.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She disapproves of rebuilding the lower quay before the wall, and she is not wrong about the sea.

relations.name: Marrow Wrack
relations.label: mason
relations.note: He knows stonework better than most on the quay and would build my stall right if the Warden let him.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Her noodle stall is by mine; we trade customers and gossip and she fed my brother all winter.

relations.name: Jory Pike
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Cheerful and owing everyone a little; he buys his supper off my stall and pays most of it.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: trade
relations.note: She knows the price of everything and I keep up with her.

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: salve-seller
relations.note: She mends the builders' hands and sells me salve for mine. She keeps her husband's quarrel with Fenwick out of the stall, which I respect.

memories.gist: The Surge took the lower quay and my mother's stall with it; we fried fish on the upper steps for a month after.
I fried my first fish at my mother's stall and sold the whole batch before the morning boats came in.
Ostrander Mackerel told me he meant to court Sella Tallow, and I told him to save for the net first.
I heard Marrow Wrack and Gideon Fenwick each call the other a cheat over a load of brick, and the carters took sides.
Ostrander Vane patched the lower quay with salvage timber and I thought, that should be stone, and said so.

stances.why: Timber went under in the Surge; stone would not have.
A working lower quay would pay for the wall twice over, and the Warden will not see it.
My mother fed the quay on credit and got little back; I keep the stall's marks in my own apron.
Wrack and Fenwick each call the other a cheat and the good stone stays in Kettlebridge for it.
He would owe the whole quay for a net; someone in the family should count.

sheet.narrative: I came down from the north shore years ago with a tarred boat and a north-shore accent the quay still laughs at, and I never went back. The outer shoals are my ground; I know their moods better than I know most men. Lyss keeps the soup stall by the tide steps, and our boy mends nets on the quay. We get by, though Ostrander Cormorant's share of the net hangs over me and the stone price keeps the quay poor.
values: paying what I owe when I can
goals: clear the net-share debt to Ostrander Cormorant
see the boy crew on a proper boat
keep the tarred boat sound another winter

relations.name: Lyss Fenner
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the stall and the house; I'd be lost without her.

relations.name: Rook Fenner the younger
relations.label: son
relations.note: Quick with a knot, that one. Wants to crew for Cormorant.

relations.name: Ostrander Cormorant
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe him for a share of a net. He's a good fisherman and a hard man.

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: friend
relations.note: A loud fool, but he knows the tides and he'll share a drink.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: buyer
relations.note: She buys my catch and pays fair, most times.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She speaks for the quay. I keep my head down when she talks of the seawall.

relations.name: Wick Cormorant
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: The boy's friend. His father's boat is better than mine.

memories.gist: I rowed down from the north shore with nothing but a tarred boat and a net, and the quay laughed at my accent.
The night the Surge came, I pulled Wick Gull's boat off the lower quay with a rope and my back.
Lyss and I set up the soup stall the week after we were married; she's run it ever since.
Ostrander Cormorant lent me a share of his net when mine tore, and I've not cleared it yet.
The boy mended his first net at seven and was quicker at it than me.

stances.why: A man who doesn't pay his debts is no better than a wrecker.
The shoals have fed us through lean times; I trust them more than the land.
The fish road is for runners and guards; my place is the boat.
The lower quay needs a wall, but I won't march for it.

sheet.secret: I've been setting aside a few marks in a jar behind the chimney to pay Cormorant before winter, and I've told no one, not even Lyss.

sheet.narrative: I keep the soup and bread stall by the tide steps, up before the early boats and last to bank the fire. Rook fishes the outer shoals and our boy mends nets on the quay. I trade with Nia Gull and buy lamp oil from Nia Brine, and I know every debt on this quay by the way people order their soup. Sella Pike feeds half the quay on credit and owes Mira Sallow for medicines; I owe Sella a little myself, and it feels like the whole quay is living on promises.
values: a hot bowl for a cold morning
goals: keep the stall solvent through the lean season
see the boy settled with a crew
clear what I owe Sella Pike without hard words

relations.name: Rook Fenner
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He's a quiet man with a good boat; I'd have no one else.

relations.name: Rook Fenner the younger
relations.label: son
relations.note: Quick with a knot and set on Cormorant's boat.

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: We trade fish and bread most mornings.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: supplier
relations.note: Her lamp oil is good and she's fair on the price.

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: She's fed half the quay on credit; I owe her a little and she's never pressed me.

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She sells medicines and knows the coughs of the quay.

relations.name: Jory Pike
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Sella's boy, cheerful and always owing someone.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She knows the price of everything, but she pays for the bread.

memories.gist: I set up the soup stall the week after Rook and I were married, with a pot borrowed from my mother.
The Surge took the lower quay and we fed the soaked families from the stall for three days.
Sella Pike gave me credit for a whole winter when Rook's boat was laid up, and I've not forgotten it.
The boy mended his first net at seven and was quicker at it than his father.
Nia Brine and I argued over the price of lamp oil and settled it over a bowl of soup.

stances.why: A cold fisherman is no good to anyone; the stall opens before dawn.
Credit is a kindness; I won't abuse it.
Sella's credit and the stone price have everyone owing everyone.
He wants Cormorant's boat, but the deep water took good men in the Surge.

sheet.narrative: I'm eleven and I mend nets on the quay, and I'm quick with a knot. Da fishes the outer shoals and Ma keeps the soup stall by the tide steps. Wick Cormorant and me play on the quay and I want to crew on his father's boat one day. The quay laughs at Da's accent, but I don't.
goals: crew on Ostrander Cormorant's boat
mend a net as fast as Da
see the outer shoals

relations.name: Rook Fenner
relations.label: father
relations.note: He fishes the outer shoals and mends nets slow.

relations.name: Lyss Fenner
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the soup stall and says the deep water took good men.

relations.name: Wick Cormorant
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play on the quay and he says I can crew with his father.

relations.name: Ostrander Cormorant
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: His boat is the best on the quay; I want to crew for him.

memories.gist: Da pulled Wick Gull's boat off the lower quay the night of the Surge, and I watched from the tide steps.
I mended my first net at seven and was quicker at it than Da.
Wick Cormorant and me raced our knots on the quay and he won, but I'm getting faster.

stances.why: I want to be a fisherman like Da, but on a bigger boat.
A good knot keeps the catch in and the boat safe.
The quay laughs at Da's north-shore accent, and I won't.

sheet.narrative: I keep the lamp-oil stall at the night market, and I have kept it alone since the Surge took my husband and the lower quay both. Oil, wicks, salt: nothing anyone can do without, and nothing I give away. The quay's stone price is robbery and the Warden knows it, but I pay my stall fee and I keep my own counsel. I trust the tide and my own count, and not much else.
values: keeping the stall and the marks it makes
independence: owe no one more than you must
the night market and the crews who trade there
her son's future on the quay
goals: keep the stall solvent through the winter
clear the debt to Bramwell Tallow for the tar
keep Tam out of the water and out of trouble
find cheap stone where the Warden does not look
sheet.mood: wary, brisk, tired behind the eyes

relations.name: Tam Harrow
relations.label: son
relations.note: He carries my loads and asks no questions, which is worth more than marks.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe him for a barrel of tar and he reminds me of it every market.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: trade neighbour
relations.note: She knows the price of everything, and so do I; we get on well enough.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: customer
relations.note: She buys my oil for the night crews and pays on time, mostly.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She speaks for the quay and collects my stall fee; I keep my head down when she walks the stalls.

relations.name: Sella Tallow
relations.label: friend of my son
relations.note: A good girl for Tam to run with; she minds her mother's stall better than most.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She set my wrist after the Surge and asked nothing for it, which I have not forgotten.

relations.name: Tam Sedge
relations.label: carrier
relations.note: He shifted a load for me and never once asked what was under the sacking; that's worth a few marks in his mother's smoke shed, and worth keeping quiet about.

memories.gist: The night the surge came I was on the stall and the water took the lower quay and my husband with it.
I opened the stall the next week because the crews still needed oil and I still needed marks.
Tam carried his first load for Bramwell Tallow last spring and came home proud with a mark in his fist.
A Sootwood woodcutter offered me stone cheap off the back of a cart, and I did not ask where it came from.
I sold that stone on the quay as salvage before the Warden's man came round the stalls.

stances.why: Everyone on the quay says they will pay; half of them do.
Kettlebridge sells us our own wall at a price that keeps the lower quay drowned.
It is the only thing between me and the poor terrace.
The quay is built on salvage; mine is no worse than anyone's.
The sea took his father and I will not give it the son as well.

sheet.secret: She buys stone from a Sootwood woodcutter who lifts it off the Kettlebridge road and sells it on the quay as salvage; she fears the Warden finding out more than she fears the woodcutter.

sheet.narrative: I carry loads for the stalls and for Bramwell Tallow, and I listen to the night crews talk about the harbour mouth and the stone price. My father drowned in the Surge before I was old enough to crew with him, so I am the man of the stall now. Sella Tallow is the only one who talks to me like I am not a child. I want a boat of my own one day, or at least a share in a catch.
values: the night crews and their talk
getting a place on a boat
goals: earn enough carrying to buy a good knife
learn the harbour mouth from the crews
keep his mother from worrying about the Warden

relations.name: Sable Harrow
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She works the stall all night and I carry for her; I do not ask her where the cheap loads come from.

relations.name: Sella Tallow
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She minds her mother's stall and knows every price on the quay; she talks to me proper.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: employer
relations.note: He pays me a mark a load and shouts if I am slow.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: She slips me a pie end when I have carried for her, and asks after my mother.

relations.name: Wick Cormorant
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He fishes with his father and says he will take me out when I am bigger.

memories.gist: The surge came at night and I woke in the loft with water in the street; my father did not come back.
I carried my first load for Bramwell Tallow and he paid me a whole mark.
I helped my mother shift a cart of stone to the stall and she told me not to say where it came from.
Sella Tallow taught me to count the night crews' bowls so her mother does not lose marks.

stances.why: My mother says the crews talk too much and the Warden listens.
Every man on the quay who has a boat has a house; every man without one is one storm from nothing.
My mother says it, and the crews say it, and the lower quay is still broken.

sheet.narrative: I came down the fish road from Kettlebridge after the Surge with my wife and daughter and what tools I could carry. I build in concrete and salvage because that's what the quay has, but I know stone, and the seawall should be stone from the ridge, not the overpriced stuff Crane sends. Gideon Fenwick took my work and slandered me, and I won't set foot in Kettlebridge while he has a yard there. I owe Josiah Crane for a load of brick, and that debt sits on me like a wet coat.
goals: build the seawall in stone from the ridge
clear my debt to Josiah Crane
see Gideon Fenwick get his due
keep my family fed and housed

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She's the only one who knows what we lost in Kettlebridge, and she still stands by me.

relations.name: Nia Wrack
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She's got her mother's sense and my stubbornness; I want better for her than a borrowed boat.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: workmate
relations.note: We patch the lower quay together and curse the stone price together.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He holds my brick debt and I can't pay it yet.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: enemy
relations.note: He took my work and slandered me; I won't forget.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She wants the seawall as much as I do, and she listens when I talk stone.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She and Odile work together; a good woman with a bone-setting hand.

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Odile trades herbs with her; she keeps a good room of salves.

relations.name: Dele Oyelaran
relations.label: old friend
relations.note: Another man who came down the road and found the door shut; we drink to it when he's down.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: quay neighbour
relations.note: She cooks a good fried fish and pays on time, but she took Fenwick's word over mine when the tale came down the fish road — I'll build her stone stall when there's stone to be had, and watch her while I do it.

memories.gist: The quarrel with Gideon Fenwick over the job and the brick load; he said I cheated him, and the whole yard heard.
Packing our things and walking down the fish road after the Surge, with Odile and Nia and a handcart of tools.
The first time I saw the lower quay after the surge: broken concrete, salt-eaten timber, and no stone anywhere.
Setting the first salvage beam on the lower quay with Ostrander Vane, and him saying we'd build it proper one day.
Borrowing the load of brick from Josiah Crane on a handshake and a promise, and the look he gave me.

stances.why: Concrete and salvage won't hold against the next surge; the ridge has good stone.
Fenwick's yard is there, and I won't give him the satisfaction.
I owe Crane for the brick, and I'll pay it even if it takes a year.
Odile and Nia are all I have left from the old life.
They sell stone dear and call it fair trade.

sheet.secret: I once took a small block of dressed stone from a Kettlebridge yard without paying, the week before we left. I tell myself it was owed wages.

sheet.narrative: I keep a healer's room behind the fish market and set the builders' bones when they fall. I came down from Kettlebridge with Marrow and Nia after the Surge, and the cold welcome we got there still stings. I know the quarrel cost us our house, and I wish Marrow would let it go, but I won't say so to his face. I want Nia settled with a man who has a roof, not a man who borrows boats.
goals: keep my family healthy and fed
see Nia married to someone steady
build up my stock of salves
avoid open quarrel with Kettlebridge

relations.name: Marrow Wrack
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He's a good man with a hard head; I wish he'd let the Fenwick quarrel lie.

relations.name: Nia Wrack
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She's got a good heart, but she doesn't see what debts can do to a household.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: colleague
relations.note: We set bones together and share what herbs we can.

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: colleague
relations.note: She knows her herbs, and she worries about the winter cough like I do.

relations.name: Ysolde Fenwick
relations.label: herb trader
relations.note: She's a strange one, but her salves are good.

relations.name: Jory Pike
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: A cheerful lad, but he owes half the quay and borrows boats.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: employer
relations.note: She keeps Nia in work at her noodle stall.

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: She's a good woman, but her son needs to stand on his own.

relations.name: Gideon Fenwick
relations.label: grudge
relations.note: His quarrel took our house and our town from us; I will not forget it, whatever Marrow says.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He patches the lower quay with salvage and wants proper stone; he took Marrow's side against Fenwick, and I remember that.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: She cooks at the fish market and wants her stall in stone; a hard worker, and she does not carry tales about my daughter.

memories.gist: The morning we left Kettlebridge: the neighbours looking away, and the cold rain on the fish road.
Setting a quarryman's leg in Kettlebridge before the Surge, and him swearing I had the gentlest hands on the ridge.
Nia's first day at Ilse Ostrander's stall, and how proud she looked with her own apron.
Marrow coming home with the brick load and the debt to Crane, and me knowing we'd be paying for it for months.
The first winter on the quay, when the cough took half the poor terrace and Mira and I ran out of salve.

stances.why: A man who borrows boats will borrow bread, and I won't have Nia go hungry.
I set bones for anyone who comes, Kettlebridge or quay, because that's what a healer does.
The quarrel cost us our house, and I wish Marrow would let it go, though I won't say so to him.
They turned their backs on us when we needed work, and I don't forget.
The winter cough takes the poor terrace every year, and I mean to have salve and fuel.

sheet.secret: I wrote to my sister in Kettlebridge last month, without telling Marrow, to ask if there was work for him there if the quarrel could be mended.

sheet.narrative: I cook at Ilse Ostrander's noodle stall and I want a stall of my own one day. Jory Pike makes me laugh and he knows boats better than anyone, but my mother measures him by his debts and I can't blame her. I like Tam Harrow too, but Jory's the one who makes me feel like the quay is a place I could belong. I wish my father would let the Kettlebridge quarrel go, but I'd never say so.
goals: save enough for my own stall
see where things go with Jory Pike
keep my parents from worrying too much
learn more recipes from Ilse

relations.name: Marrow Wrack
relations.label: father
relations.note: He's stubborn as stone, but he'd do anything for me.

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She wants me settled, and she's probably right, but she doesn't see how Jory makes me laugh.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: employer
relations.note: She's taught me most of what I know about a noodle pot.

relations.name: Jory Pike
relations.label: suitor
relations.note: He's cheerful and he knows boats, and he makes me feel like the quay is home.

relations.name: Tam Harrow
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He's a good lad, but he's not Jory.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We work the stalls together and she knows everyone's business.

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Jory's mother is kind, but she worries about him like I do.

relations.name: Rook Fenner the younger
relations.label: acquaintance
relations.note: Tam's cousin; a quiet lad with quick hands for a knot.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She sets bones and trades gossip with my mother; a kind woman with a sharp eye.

memories.gist: The first time I cooked a whole pot of noodles at Ilse's stall without burning them, and she nodded once.
Jory Pike bringing me a handful of harbour flowers and not knowing where to look.
My mother setting a fisherman's arm in our room while I held the lamp and tried not to look.
The night the tide lanterns were lit late and a boat came in wrong; my father cursing the wardens.
Walking the fish road with my father when I was small, before the Surge, and him showing me the ridge stone.

stances.why: I won't cook at someone else's fire forever.
He makes me laugh and he's kind, and debts can be paid.
My parents came down the road for me, and I won't shame them.
I won't say what I think about the Kettlebridge quarrel; it only makes my father angry.
A hot bowl on a cold night is worth more than a mark in the box.

sheet.secret: I've been putting aside a few marks each week for a stall of my own, and I haven't told my mother, because she'd want it for the winter store.

sheet.narrative: I fish the harbour from a boat that isn't mine, and I owe half the quay a little and pay most of it back when the catch is good. My mother has fed me on credit all my life, and now I'm courting Nia Wrack, and her mother looks at me like a bad tide. I'm cheerful about it, mostly. The debts will sort themselves out; a man with a good arm and a borrowed boat can always find work on the water.
values: keeping cheerful when the tide turns
paying what I owe, most of it, eventually
the harbour and the people in it
goals: ask Nia Wrack properly, with her mother's blessing if I can get it
pay off what I owe Wick Gull and the rest
save enough for a net of my own, maybe a boat
help my mother clear her debt to Mira Sallow
sheet.mood: hopeful, a little anxious about Odile Wrack's cold eye

relations.name: Sella Pike
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She's fed me on credit since I could hold a line; I should be paying her back, not courting.

relations.name: Nia Wrack
relations.label: sweetheart
relations.note: Quick with a joke and quicker with a ladle; I'd ask her tomorrow if her mother would have me.

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: her mother
relations.note: She looks at me and sees a debt with legs. I'll win her round or die trying.

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: I owe him for a share of a catch, and he crews me when my boat's laid up. He's loud but fair.

relations.name: Ostrander Mackerel
relations.label: drinking friend
relations.note: Good lad, saving for his own net. We drink and complain about the stone price together.

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: my mother's creditor
relations.note: She's kind enough, but she keeps the tally, and the tally's got my mother's name on it.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: Cooks a good fried fish and knows the price of everything. Nia's friendly with her.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: Harbour Warden
relations.note: She speaks for the quay, but my mother says the poor terrace should be fed before any seawall.

relations.name: Lyss Fenner
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: Her soup stall's by the tide steps where the early boats come in; she knows who's paid and who hasn't, and she's never once dunned my mother for it.

memories.gist: The night the surge came, I was out on the harbour mouth and rowed back through the wreckage of the lower quay; I pulled a neighbour's boy out of the water and never found his father.
My mother's stall at the tide steps, the smell of frying fish and the way she'd slip a bowl to anyone who looked hungry, no marks asked.
The first time Nia Wrack laughed at one of my jokes and didn't stop, at Ilse Ostrander's noodle stall after the night crews came in.
Wick Gull's boat laid up, so I crewed for him a whole season and learned the deep water past the harbour mouth; I still owe him a share of one catch.
My mother took to her bed with the cough last winter and Mira Sallow's medicines pulled her through; I heard her tell Mira she'd pay when the season turned.

stances.why: A man who pays nothing gets no boat lent to him twice.
My mother fed half the quay on credit; that's how it's done, and it comes back round.
Nia won't go against Odile Wrack, and I wouldn't ask her to.
I've been behind before and the tide always brought something in.
My mother says it, and she's right; a wall doesn't fill a belly.

sheet.narrative: I've kept a fried-fish stall by the tide steps for thirty years and fed half the quay on credit, and now the lean season has come round and I'm the one who owes. Mira Sallow's medicines kept me breathing through the winter and I haven't paid her a mark of it. My Jory is a good lad with a borrowed boat and a sweetheart, and I wish he'd ask the girl properly instead of leaving me to watch Odile Wrack's face. The stall-keepers are starting to talk about who pays and who doesn't, and I can hear my name in it.
values: the quay's poor before any seawall
paying my debts, though I can't bring myself to dun my neighbours
goals: pay Mira Sallow what I owe her for the medicines
see Jory ask Nia Wrack properly, with her mother's leave
keep the stall going through the lean weeks
stop the stall-keepers' talk before it hardens
sheet.mood: weary, proud, quietly ashamed of the tally

relations.name: Jory Pike
relations.label: son
relations.note: A good lad with a borrowed boat; I wish he'd pay off a debt before he courts one.

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: Her medicines kept me breathing and I can't look her in the eye till I've paid.

relations.name: Nia Wrack
relations.label: my son's sweetheart
relations.note: A hard worker and a good cook; she'd steady him, if her mother would have him.

relations.name: Odile Wrack
relations.label: her mother
relations.note: She counts every mark my Jory owes and never counts the ones he's paid.

relations.name: Lyss Fenner
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: We trade soup and fried fish across the tide steps and neither of us keeps a tally.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She set my wrist when I fell on the steps and never asked for payment.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: Harbour Warden
relations.note: She wants her seawall; I want the poor terrace fed first, and I've said so.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: Her noodle stall and mine have fed the night crews for years; we don't talk about who owes.

relations.name: Ostrander Mackerel
relations.label: young fisher
relations.note: He's eaten at my stall since he was a boy crewing for Cormorant; a steady lad, and he pays what he can when he can.

relations.name: Sella Mackerel
relations.label: stall neighbour
relations.note: We share a name and a trade and the same tide steps; she fries her fish and I fry mine, and we've never once quarrelled over a customer.

memories.gist: The surge took the lower quay and the houses on it, and I fried fish all night for the families who came up the steps with nothing but what they stood in.
The winter the cough took me, Mira Sallow came with her medicines three times and wouldn't take a mark; I told her I'd pay when the season turned.
Jory's father drowned before the surge, and I raised the boy on the stall, teaching him to gut a fish before he could read.
The lean season when the boats came in light and I kept feeding the crews on credit, telling myself the quay pays its debts.
The first time Jory brought Nia Wrack to the stall and she ate two bowls and laughed at his jokes, and I saw he was lost.

stances.why: A hungry neighbour is a debt you pay with a bowl, not a tally.
I've fed half the quay on credit; I won't be the one who turns the talk ugly.
A wall doesn't fill a belly; the Warden should feed the terrace first.
Jory needs someone to count the marks with him, and Nia Wrack is that someone.
I'll pay Mira Sallow before the stall-keepers can say I didn't.

sheet.secret: I've been selling the stall's best fish cheap to Lyss Fenner under the counter so I can put by a few marks for Mira without anyone seeing me save.

sheet.narrative: I've run my cart of salt and dried fish along this shore since I was old enough to push it, and I know every stall-keeper from the tide steps to the far end of the market. The quay buys fish and sells it back to itself twice before noon, and I take my share in the middle of that, honestly enough. Mara Quell's stall fee is due and I'll pay it when the cart comes back full, not before. Bramwell Tallow can have the rope trade; I'll keep the salt.
values: a fair price, paid and taken
the quay looks after its own
goals: clear the stall fee owed to Mara Quell
keep the salt-fish trade with the Reedmoor reed-cutters steady
see the seawall built so the lower quay trades again

relations.name: Dory Sedge
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She smokes it, I sell it; we've never needed to say which of us is the better trader.

relations.name: Tam Sedge
relations.label: son
relations.note: Good lad in the shed, but he won't go near the harbour after dark and I don't push him.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: Warden
relations.note: She holds the stall fee over me like a net over a fish. I owe it; I'll pay it.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He'd sell rope to a drowning man and charge him for the knot.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Her lamp oil and dried fish move well beside mine at the morning stalls.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Knows the price of everything on the quay, and most of the time she's right.

relations.name: Eadric Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: His reed-bed salt fish fills my cart cheap and never spoils.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Patches the lower quay with salvage and swears at the Kettlebridge price. I'd do the same.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: The Reedmoor reed-cutters send salt fish through her; we've done well by it.

memories.gist: The night the surge came, I hauled my cart up the slip and watched the lower quay go under; I lost a season's salt in the water.
The morning I first took Eadric Sedge's salt fish on the cart and sold the lot before the bells.
Bramwell Tallow cornered the rope trade and told me to my face the cart men should stick to fish.
Tam was born in the room over the smoke shed and Dory was back at the stalls inside a week.

stances.why: A trader who doesn't pay his stall fee is a trader nobody sells to.
The lower quay went under once; it will go under again, and my cart with it.
They send us stone at a price that keeps the wall unbuilt, and call it trade.
Everything I own keeps because I salt it and wait; that's the whole of my trade.

sheet.narrative: I've smoked fish in the shed behind the market for near twenty years, and the morning stalls know my smoke by the smell of it. Brannock carts what I smoke and I keep the shed and the boy and the fire. The cough goes round the poor terrace every winter and I've buried neighbours from it. I'd feed the whole quay if the shed held more.
values: feed people before you count marks
the poor terrace is still the quay
goals: keep the smoke shed and the morning stall paying
see the winter cough off the poor terrace
keep Tam out of the night harbour

relations.name: Brannock Sedge
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He carts and haggles; I smoke and keep the fire. It's worked this long.

relations.name: Tam Sedge
relations.label: son
relations.note: He's a good hand in the shed and I won't have him feared into the dark water.

relations.name: Nia Brine
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: We trade oil for smoke and worry over the same coughs.

relations.name: Maren Vane
relations.label: healer
relations.note: When the cough takes the terrace, she's the one I send for.

relations.name: Mira Sallow
relations.label: healer
relations.note: Her herbs and salves have kept more than one shed family through a winter.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: Warden
relations.note: She wants the wall; I want the poor terrace fed. Both can be true.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Her noodle stall buys my smoked fish and never once haggled me down.

relations.name: Perrin Tallow
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: Sharp on price, but she'll lend you her apron if yours is burning.

memories.gist: The surge took the shed roof and half the smoke racks; I rebuilt the racks from salvage before the fish rotted.
Tam was small when the cough went round the terrace, and I sat up nights with the neighbours' children as well as my own.
The first morning my smoked fish sold out at the stall before the sun was over the masts.
Nia Brine and I split a barrel of lamp oil when neither of us had the marks for a whole one.

stances.why: I've seen what an empty pot does to a house, and the seawall won't fill it.
My name is on every fish I sell at the morning stalls.
Wolves and stone prices don't kill half so many on this quay as the winter cough.
The harbour at night took my uncle and I'll not have it take Tam.

sheet.narrative: I help Mam in the smoke shed, turning the racks and keeping the fire low, and I know the smell of fish smoke better than I know my letters. Da lets me ride the cart sometimes when it goes no further than the morning stalls. I don't like the harbour when it's dark; the water makes noises like breathing. Dory Gull and me play under the stalls where the lamps don't reach.
goals: be trusted with the whole smoke rack
not go down to the harbour at night

relations.name: Dory Sedge
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me keep the fire low and says I've a good hand for it.

relations.name: Brannock Sedge
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lets me ride the cart when it's only the morning stalls.

relations.name: Dory Gull
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play under the stalls where the lamps don't reach.

relations.name: Sable Harrow
relations.label: stallkeeper
relations.note: She gave me a mark to carry a crate and didn't say what was in it.

memories.gist: The night the water came over the lower quay, Da carried me up the slip and Mam's shed roof came off.
The first time Mam let me turn the racks by myself and the fish came out brown and sweet.

stances.why: It makes noises like breathing and I stay up by the lamps.
She says a low fire smokes sweet, and she's never wrong about fish.

sheet.narrative: I mended nets on this quay before the lower quay was taken, and I still mend them now, though my hands are slower and the twine costs more than it did. I no longer go out; Wick's boat is his, and I watch it come in from the steps. Every name the Surge took is written in my head as well as on Ostrander Sallow's list, and I read it over when the tide lanterns are lit. Kettlebridge sold us stone at a price that would have built the wall twice over, and I do not forget it.
values: a net mended is a boat saved
the quay owes nothing to those who never shared a boat
goals: see the tide lanterns lit for every name on the list
keep Wick's boat in nets and out of debt
see a seawall built before another surge takes the rest of the lower quay
sheet.mood: quiet, weathered, slow to anger but slow to forgive

relations.name: Wick Gull
relations.label: nephew
relations.note: My brother's boy. He fishes the harbour mouth like his father did, and I mend his nets for nothing.

relations.name: Nia Gull
relations.label: niece by marriage
relations.note: A good cook and a hard worker. She feeds the night crews and never asks a mark of me.

relations.name: Dory Gull
relations.label: great-niece
relations.note: A little thing, afraid of the dark water. I tell her the lanterns keep it back.

relations.name: Ostrander Cormorant
relations.label: customer
relations.note: He pays on time for his nets, which is more than most. A hard man but a fair one.

relations.name: Ostrander Sallow
relations.label: fellow keeper
relations.note: We keep the tide lantern list between us. He writes the names; I remember the boats.

relations.name: Mara Quell
relations.label: warden
relations.note: She lost her brother as I lost mine. She wants the wall; I want it too, but I doubt she will get the stone.

relations.name: Bramwell Tallow
relations.label: chandler
relations.note: His rope and tar are good, but he never forgets a mark owed.

relations.name: Josiah Crane
relations.label: stone-seller
relations.note: He sold us stone at a price that would have built the wall twice. I do not care what his reasons were.

relations.name: Wick Brine
relations.label: night guard
relations.note: He walks the road at night and knows the smugglers' paths. A useful man to have about the quay.

relations.name: Ostrander Vane
relations.label: builder
relations.note: Patches the lower quay with salvage and wants proper stone; a good lad with a bad job.

relations.name: Rennick Vane
relations.label: quay guard
relations.note: Walks the road with the runners; I'd trust him with a net or a name.

relations.name: Ilse Ostrander
relations.label: stall-keeper
relations.note: Her noodle stall has fed me many a cold night; her boy Kai is another matter.

relations.name: Kai Ostrander
relations.label: deserter
relations.note: Went off and left the quay guard; I do not hold with a man who runs.

memories.gist: The night the Surge came, I stood on the upper steps and watched the lower quay go under, and counted the boats that did not come back.
My brother Gull taught me to mend a net before I could row, and I have mended them every day since.
When Wick's father drowned, I took the boy on the steps and showed him how to hold a needle, because there was nothing else I could give him.
Ostrander Sallow and I sat up one winter night writing the drowned list fair, and I named every boat I could remember for him to write.
I went up the fish road once to Kettlebridge to ask about stone, and came back with nothing but a price I could not pay.

stances.why: Every name on the tide lantern list is a boat I knew and a person the quay lost.
The quay's way: you owe nothing to anyone who has not shared a boat with you.
The wall is unbuilt because their stone is dear, and the lower quay stays broken.
A mended net saves a boat; talk saves nothing.
A light lit late is a boat lost. I have seen it.

villages.name: Elmwick
villages.character: a farming village by the water
villages.ledger: Elmwick. The Lakemead was Elmwick's common before anyone let it.

sheet.narrative: I am Hob Garrow, elder of Elmwick, and I have farmed these strips since I was a boy. I grazed the Lakemead when it was common, and I will not sit quiet while Nell Sedge lets it to strangers. My daughter Annot keeps the house and works the north strips with me, and my wife Leofgifu keeps the cook-fire. I am slow to part with marks, but I pay what I owe.
goals: press Elmwick's claim to the Lakemead
settle the quarrel between Oswin Wray and Pike Tarn
see the village through the winter
keep the Garrow strips in the family

relations.name: Annot Garrow
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She works the strips with me and keeps the house; I lean on her more than I say.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the cook-fire and the common bake; I would be lost without her.

relations.name: Cerdic Garrow
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: The boy helps with the goats and the harvest; he will make a farmer.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: rival
relations.note: She had no right to let the Lakemead; it was Elmwick's common.

relations.name: Jem Coombe
relations.label: trespasser
relations.note: He farms the meadow that should be ours and pays her rent.

relations.name: Oswin Wray
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A good hunter, but he and Pike Tarn quarrel over traps.

relations.name: Pike Tarn
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He hunts the southern woods and says Oswin takes his game.

relations.name: Aldwyn Bexley
relations.label: builder
relations.note: He repaired my barn; I owe him for the work but have not paid yet.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: Thornby's headman; I know him by name only.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Annot is close with her; the small folk are good neighbours.

relations.name: Cuthbert Stave
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: A Thornby man, but he knows the southern woods and keeps his quarrels honest; I'd have him at the common table.

relations.name: Edric Toller
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Farms the Toller acres by the stream and grumbles about the Lakemead quarrel as I do; a steady man.

relations.name: Goda Toller
relations.label: neighbour's daughter
relations.note: Edric's girl works the fields and wants a strip of her own; she'd farm the Lakemead right if we win it back.

relations.name: Nerys Bexley
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: Aldwyn's wife keeps the Bexley plot and hens; a quay woman learning our fields, and doing well enough.

relations.name: Odelia Harrow
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: A Ferncross woodcutter; she trades timber with our builders, but I know her only by her loads.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar
relations.note: The small-folk pedlar on the east road; he trades with Nell Sedge, but he's civil and brings news.

memories.gist: As a boy I grazed our goats on the Lakemead with the other Elmwick lads; it was common then.
When Nell Sedge let the Lakemead to the Coombes, I told her to her face it was never Reedmoor's to let.
Aldwyn Bexley repaired our barn after the storm; I have not yet found the marks to pay him.
I heard Oswin Wray and Pike Tarn accuse each other of poaching; I want peace in the village.
The Lean Year was hard; we ate thin and the wolves came close.

stances.why: I grazed it as a boy and it was always common.
A man's word is his bond, but marks are hard to come by.
Quarrels between neighbours weaken us all.
Nell Sedge took what was not hers.

sheet.narrative: I am Annot Garrow, Hob's daughter, and I work the north strips with my father. My husband was a fisher, lost in the Surge, and I raise our son Cerdic alone. I keep the house and trade eggs with Tern Gannet when she comes through. I miss my husband, but the fields do not wait.
goals: raise Cerdic well
see the Garrow strips prosper
keep the house in order
trade eggs for what we need

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: father
relations.note: He is stubborn about the Lakemead, but he is my father and I work beside him.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps the cook-fire and the common bake; she is the heart of the village.

relations.name: Cerdic Garrow
relations.label: son
relations.note: My boy; he helps with the goats and the harvest.

relations.name: Tern Gannet
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She carries fish down the road; I trade eggs with her.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: close friend
relations.note: We understand each other; she lost people too.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: rival
relations.note: My father says she had no right to the Lakemead; I keep my distance.

relations.name: Thea Wray
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: The child has a cough; I hope she recovers.

relations.name: Sibley Toller
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She knows healing; she has been watching Thea.

memories.gist: My husband drowned in the Surge two winters ago; I still wake thinking I hear him.
Cerdic was born on a cold morning; my mother delivered him.
I trade eggs with Tern Gannet when she comes down the fish road; she always has news.
Mallow Bramblecap came to sit with me after my husband died; we have been close since.
The Elmwick men pulled down the Coombes' fence twice; I stayed out of it.

stances.why: Cerdic and my parents are all I have.
The land is our living.
Mallow and I help each other through.
It is my father's fight; I have enough to do.

sheet.narrative: I am Cerdic. I help my mother with the goats and the harvest, and I play with Fennel Underbank when the small folk come. I miss my father, but I do not remember him well. I like the goats and the fields.
goals: help with the goats
play with Fennel
learn to be a farmer

relations.name: Annot Garrow
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She works the fields and keeps me safe.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: grandfather
relations.note: He teaches me about the goats and the harvest.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She bakes bread and tells stories.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We play together when the small folk come.

relations.name: Thea Wray
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She has a cough; I hope she gets better.

memories.gist: My father drowned in the Surge; I remember his boat and his laugh.
I helped my mother with the goats when one was sick; she said I was a good hand.
I played with Fennel Underbank in the meadow; we caught frogs.

sheet.narrative: I am Leofgifu Garrow, Hob's wife, and I keep the village cook-fire and the common bake. I cook for the common table and trade bread with Tansy Sedge. I worry about the winter store, and I keep an eye on Thea Wray's cough. My daughter Annot works the strips with my husband, and my grandson Cerdic is a joy.
goals: keep the winter store full
see Thea Wray recover
bake for the common table
trade bread for what we need

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is stubborn, but he is a good man.

relations.name: Annot Garrow
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She works hard and raises Cerdic well.

relations.name: Cerdic Garrow
relations.label: grandson
relations.note: He helps with the goats and makes me laugh.

relations.name: Tansy Sedge
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: She trades bread with me; a good woman.

relations.name: Thea Wray
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: The child has a cough; I have offered remedies.

relations.name: Rowan Wray
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She treats Thea with herbs; I hope it is enough.

relations.name: Sibley Toller
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She knows healing; we both watch Thea.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: friend
relations.note: Annot is close with her; the small folk are good neighbours.

relations.name: Nell Sedge
relations.label: rival
relations.note: My husband quarrels with her over the Lakemead; I keep out of it.

relations.name: Oswin Wray
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He hunts the woods for his family and frets over Thea's cough; I keep an eye on the child and say nothing to worry him further.

memories.gist: I have kept the village cook-fire for thirty years; I know every family's portion.
The Lean Year was hard; I stretched every loaf and we still went hungry.
I delivered Cerdic with my own hands; he was a big baby.
I traded bread with Tansy Sedge at the market; she always has good fish.
I have watched Thea Wray's cough since spring; I fear it is the winter cough.

stances.why: The common table is the heart of Elmwick.
We cannot afford another lean year.
I have some medicine knowledge and I use it.
Hob, Annot and Cerdic are my world.

sheet.narrative: I keep the wolves off the Elmwick paths and the meat on the village table. The woods are my ledger: every trap, every track, every debt. Pike Tarn has been setting his snares too close to the village, and I have told Hob Garrow so. My Thea coughs and I cannot trap that.
goals: Keep the southern woods clear of wolves
See Pike Tarn's snares moved off the village paths
Find a healer who can help Thea

relations.name: Rowan Wray
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She knows the streams and I know the woods; between us we keep the house.

relations.name: Thea Wray
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She has her mother's quick hands and my stubbornness. The cough frightens me more than any wolf.

relations.name: Pike Tarn
relations.label: rival
relations.note: He sets his lines too close to the paths and calls it hunting. The wolves will come for the village, not his pride.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: elder
relations.note: I have told him about Pike. He listens, but he is slow to act.

relations.name: Cuthbert Stave
relations.label: friend
relations.note: A good hunter from Thornby. We understand each other without many words.

relations.name: Sibley Toller
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She knows herbs and has a steady hand. Rowan trusts her, and so do I.

relations.name: Aethelred Tanner
relations.label: buyer
relations.note: He drives a hard bargain for hides, but he pays.

relations.name: Marta Hale
relations.label: outlaw
relations.note: Her people stole my trap. They are not farmers anymore, whatever they say.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: elder's wife
relations.note: She keeps the common bake and the cook-fire, and she has been good to Thea — sends her broth and asks after her cough. I am grateful, though I would rather not hear the worry in her voice.

memories.gist: The Lean Year: the wolves came down bold and I sat up three nights by the sheep fold with a spear.
The day Thea was born, I was out tracking a wounded boar and came home to a daughter.
Finding my best trap gone from the south line and Coldwell boot prints in the mud.
Pike Tarn's snare line set not fifty paces from the village path, and a wolf track beside it.
Thea's cough started after the spring rains and has not left her since.

stances.why: A hunter who lets wolves near the paths is no hunter.
He is drawing wolves to the village and taking game from my lines.
Thea's cough and Rowan's worry are heavier than any quarrel.
They stole my trap and rob carriers on the road.
The woods have rules. People make excuses.

sheet.narrative: I fish the forest streams and smoke the catch for the village, and I know every pool and eddy better than anyone. But my Thea has coughed since the spring, and no stream herb will shift it. Sibley Toller fears it may be the winter cough. I am frightened, and I do not like asking the village for help.
goals: See Thea well again
Keep the smokehouse going
Find a remedy that works

relations.name: Oswin Wray
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He hunts harder when he is worried. I know what it means.

relations.name: Thea Wray
relations.label: daughter
relations.note: She is cross and tired and wants to be out. I keep her by the fire and it breaks my heart.

relations.name: Sibley Toller
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She has some healing knowledge and fears the winter cough. I trust her, though I am slow to ask.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She keeps the common bake and knows the village's ills. She would help if asked.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: trade partner
relations.note: The small-folk pedlar takes my smoked fish and brings news. He knows the east road.

relations.name: Pike Tarn
relations.label: stranger
relations.note: Oswin's quarrel with him is Oswin's. I keep to the streams.

memories.gist: Thea's first cough after the spring rains, and how it has lingered all summer.
Smoking a fine catch of trout with Thea helping, before the cough took her strength.
The day the Kettlebridge smoke drifted east and soured the drying fish; I had to throw half the catch away.
Sibley Toller telling me the cough might be the winter cough that has been going round.
Oswin coming home late from hunting, worried, and saying he would go to Tanglewood for a healer if he knew the way.

stances.why: She is my daughter and I will try anything.
She knows herbs and fears the same thing I do.
We have always managed alone, and I do not want pity.
It drifts east and ruins the drying fish.
The pools have never lied to me, unlike people.

sheet.narrative: I am tired and cross and my chest hurts when I cough. Mother keeps me by the fire and I want to be out with Cerdic and the goats. I mend nets but my hands are slow now.
goals: To feel better and go out to play

relations.name: Oswin Wray
relations.label: father
relations.note: He brings me feathers from the woods and tells me about the tracks.

relations.name: Rowan Wray
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She keeps me by the fire and makes me drink bitter herbs. I know she is frightened.

relations.name: Cerdic Garrow
relations.label: friend
relations.note: He plays with me when I am allowed out. I miss running with him.

relations.name: Sibley Toller
relations.label: healer
relations.note: She looks at my chest and speaks quietly to Mother. I do not like it.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: village cook
relations.note: She keeps the common bake and gave me a warm heel of bread when Mother took me to the fire. She looks at me the way Mother does now, and I wish she would not.

memories.gist: Running with Cerdic Garrow along the stream path before the cough came.
The first time I coughed so hard I could not catch my breath, and Mother held me.
Sibley Toller listening to my back with a cold hand and saying something to Mother I was not meant to hear.

sheet.narrative: I came up from Lanternquay after the Surge with Nerys and Merek, and Elmwick has been good to us — Hob Garrow gave me work when no one else would. I build and repair what I can: barns, houses, the odd bridge. I'm proud of the Garrow barn, but I took Osric Dunn's timber on credit to finish it and the debt is due at the next market, and I haven't the marks. I keep hoping Hob will pay me enough to clear it, but I'm ashamed I may have to ask for more time.
goals: clear the timber debt to Osric Dunn
get paid for the Garrow barn
keep my family fed and housed
build something that lasts

relations.name: Nerys Bexley
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the marks and knows we're short; I should have told her about the timber.

relations.name: Merek Bexley
relations.label: son
relations.note: Born on the quay, still scared of the woods. I want him to feel at home here.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: employer
relations.note: He gave me work when we arrived. I hope he'll pay me enough to clear the debt.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He let me take the timber on credit. I owe him and I don't want to shame myself.

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: friend
relations.note: A good sort, works fallen wood like me. We understand each other.

memories.gist: The Surge took our house on the lower quay; we escaped with what we could carry.
Hob Garrow hired me to fix his barn when no one else would.
I finished the Garrow barn and it stands straight and true.
I took Osric Dunn's timber on credit, and the debt is due at the next market.
Merek was born on the quay, and the first time he saw the deep woods he clung to my leg.

stances.why: A good name is worth more than marks, and I won't be known as a man who doesn't pay.
Nerys and Merek are all I have; everything I do is for them.
I've seen the quay; Kettlebridge will never sell stone cheap enough to build a wall.
It's what I know, and Elmwick always needs building and mending.

sheet.secret: I haven't told Nerys how short we are; I'm afraid she'll be angry I took the timber without asking.

sheet.narrative: I keep the Bexley plot and the hens, and I trade eggs at the market. I'm a Lanternquay woman learning the fields, and I miss the quay and the tide lanterns every day. I keep the household's marks in a locked box and I know exactly how short we are. Aldwyn took Osric Dunn's timber on credit without telling me, and I'm angry and scared we'll lose our good name.
goals: keep the household's marks safe
see the debt to Osric Dunn paid
make a home in Elmwick
maybe see the quay again one day

relations.name: Aldwyn Bexley
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He's a good man, but he should have told me about the timber before he took it.

relations.name: Merek Bexley
relations.label: son
relations.note: He's still afraid of the woods; I try to make him feel safe.

relations.name: Leofgifu Garrow
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She's been kind to me since we came; I can talk to her.

relations.name: Osric Dunn
relations.label: creditor
relations.note: He's owed for the timber, and I don't want to shame us by not paying.

relations.name: Hob Garrow
relations.label: employer
relations.note: He's Aldwyn's work, and I hope he pays enough to clear the debt.

memories.gist: The Surge took our home on the lower quay; we lost everything but each other.
I learned to keep hens in Elmwick, though I still miss the tide lanterns.
Aldwyn told me he'd taken the timber on credit, and I found we were short of marks.
Leofgifu Garrow showed me how to trade eggs at the market.

stances.why: I keep the household's marks in a locked box; we can't afford to lose them.
Aldwyn should have told me about the debt; we're supposed to be partners.
